jobs.title: Project Manager
jobs.description:
Your Job

John Zink, a leader in the vapor control industry and part of Koch Engineering Solutions (KES) company, is looking to add a Project Manager to our dynamic team. This position is located in Tulsa, OK and offers an exciting opportunity to be part of a growing project management team — something we consider a significant advantage as it reflects our expanding capabilities and increasing market demand.

As a Project Manager, you would manage projects related to emission control solutions in the vapor control or biogas markets. If you are a proactive and results-driven professional with a passion for project management, we want to hear from you!

You will work directly with our clients to ensure communication, project updates and resolution to any issues or project changes. It will be critical that you cultivate relationships within multi-discipline engineering teams, executives, stakeholders, and suppliers to track project milestones and key deliverables. You will also be responsible for concurrent projects with accountability over designs, schedules, and budgets.

This role is not eligible for VISA sponsorship.

What You Will Do

Plan, execute, and manage projects from initiation to completion, ensuring adherence to budget, timeline, and quality standards.
Lead cross-functional teams (including individuals on site in Tulsa and globally remote) to define project scope, objectives, and deliverables. Foster a positive team environment, promoting collaboration, accountability, and motivation.
Effectively align stakeholders to achieve superior results.
Develop project plans, schedules, resource allocation, and risk assessment.
Continuously analyze project progress, identify potential roadblocks, and implement necessary corrective actions.
Communicate effectively with internal and external stakeholders, providing regular project status updates and managing expectations.
Conduct post-project evaluations to identify lessons learned and implement improvements for future projects.

Who You Are (Basic Qualifications)

Experience applying project management methodologies, tools, and techniques
Experience leading projects or cross-functional teams with responsibility for budgets, schedules, and deliverables.
Ability to travel up to 10%.
Must have legal authorization to work permanently in the United States for any employer without requiring a visa transfer or visa sponsorship.

What Will Put You Ahead

Knowledge and understanding of packaged combustions equipment, vapor combustion units, vapor recovery units, biogas systems, or similar.
Experience with engineered and fabricated products.
Experience in an engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) organization.
Bachelor's degree in Engineering preferred.
PMP certification or equivalent.

At Koch companies, we are entrepreneurs. This means we openly challenge the status quo, find new ways to create value and get rewarded for our individual contributions. Any compensation range provided for a role is an estimate determined by available market data. The actual amount may be higher or lower than the range provided considering each candidate's knowledge, skills, abilities, and geographic location. If you have questions, please speak to your recruiter about the flexibility and detail of our compensation philosophy.

Hiring Philosophy

All Koch companies value diversity of thought, perspectives, aptitudes, experiences, and backgrounds. We are Military Ready and Second Chance employers. Learn more about our hiring philosophy here.

Who We Are

As a Koch Engineered Solutions company, John Zink is a global leader in emissions control and a pioneer in modern Combustion solutions. Our research and development facilities make up the largest testing complex of its kind. Additionally, our worldwide service organization is the largest, most technically advanced team of its kind. We provide solutions to capture emissions, destroy pollutants, manage waste and heat vital processes to help industries operate more cleanly and efficiently.

At Koch, employees are empowered to do what they do best to make life better. Learn how our business philosophy helps employees unleash their potential while creating value for themselves and the company.

Our Benefits

Our goal is for each employee, and their families, to live fulfilling and healthy lives. We provide essential resources and support to build and maintain physical, financial, and emotional strength - focusing on overall wellbeing so you can focus on what matters most. Our benefits plan includes - medical, dental, vision, flexible spending and health savings accounts, life insurance, ADD, disability, retirement, paid vacation/time off, educational assistance, and may also include infertility assistance, paid parental leave and adoption assistance. Specific eligibility criteria is set by the applicable Summary Plan Description, policy or guideline and benefits may vary by geographic region. If you have questions on what benefits apply to you, please speak to your recruiter.

Additionally, everyone has individual work and personal needs. We seek to enable the best work environment that helps you and the business work together to produce superior results.

Equal Opportunities

Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability and protected veteran status. Except where prohibited by state law, some offers of employment are conditioned upon successfully passing a drug test. jobs.title: MCU Offshore Project Manager
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary

En tant qu’équipement client, installations ou projets d’infrastructure connexes : responsable de l'exécution du projet, de la comptabilité des résultats et de la satisfaction de la clientèle par la gestion des activités et des ressources liées au projet. Exerce un impact sur les approches, projets et programmes du domaine fonctionnel ou de l'organisation et des méthodes de travail affectées. Influe sur la qualité, l'efficacité et l'efficience de sa propre équipe. Contribue significativement à l'élaboration des priorités. Se fonde sur des pratiques et des politiques professionnelles façonnées par le rôle. Le rôle dispose d'une autonomie modérée, nécessitant un haut niveau de discernement opérationnel.

Job Description

Rôles et responsabilités

Projets non clés en main ou projets portant uniquement sur des produits/équipements. Responsable de la supervision du projet et de la direction et/ou de la gestion directe ou indirecte des ressources du projet pour les projets de petite et moyenne taille (taille relative à GE) pouvant inclure des équipements uniquement, des suites de produits ou des projets non clés en main.
Développer des connaissances spécialisées dans sa discipline. Prodigue ses conseils en matière de meilleures pratiques et/ou de qualité. Est conscient des derniers développements techniques dans son propre domaine. Contribue à l'élaboration de stratégies et de politiques, et assure la mise en œuvre dans les limites de son domaine de responsabilités.
Possède une connaissance approfondie des meilleures pratiques et de la manière dont son propre domaine s'intègre aux autres. Possède une connaissance pratique de la concurrence et des facteurs qui les différencient sur le marché.
Fait preuve de discernement pour prendre des décisions ou résoudre des tâches ou des problèmes moyennement complexes dans les domaines de l'exploitation, de la gestion des produits, de la fabrication, de la technologie ou de l'ingénierie. Adopte une nouvelle perspective sur les solutions existantes. Utilise son expérience technique et son expertise en analyse de données pour appuyer les recommandations. Fait appel à des ressources limitées internes et externes en dehors de sa propre fonction pour l'aider à prendre une décision.
Agit en tant que ressource pour ses collègues moins expérimentés. Peut piloter de petits projets avec des risques et des besoins en ressources modérés. Explique les informations difficiles ou sensibles. S'efforce d'établir un consensus. Développe les compétences de persuasion nécessaires pour influencer les autres sur des sujets relevant de son domaine.

Qualifications De Base

Pour les rôles en dehors des États-Unis - Ce rôle nécessite une expérience avancée de la fonction et de la station de travail audio numérique. Connaissances de niveau équivalent à une maîtrise dans une université accréditée (ou un baccalauréat avec une expérience dans un domaine pertinent).
Pour les rôles aux États-Unis - Maîtrise d'une université accrédité (ou diplôme d'études secondaires et/ou diplôme d'étude général avec au moins 6 ans d'expérience dans la fonction).

Caractéristiques souhaitées

Solides compétences en communication orale et écrite. Solides compétences relationnelles et de leadership. Capacité démontrée d'analyse et de résolution des problèmes. Capacité démontrée à diriger des programmes/projets. Capacité à documenter, planifier, lancer et exécuter des programmes. Compétences établies en gestion de projet.Remarque : Pour se conformer aux exigences légales américaines en matière d'immigration et autres, il est nécessaire de préciser le nombre minimum d'années d'expérience requis pour tout poste basé aux États-Unis. Pour les rôles en dehors des États-Unis, pour assurer la conformité avec la législation applicable, les juristes doivent mentionner le niveau d'expérience requis et non PAS un nombre minimum d'années.Cette description de poste a pour but de fournir un guide détaillé du rôle. Toutefois, il n'est pas prévu de modifier ou de restreindre et/ou d'élargir de quelque manière que ce soit les tâches requises de chaque employé, telles qu'elles sont définies dans leur contrat de travail respectif et/ou convenues d'un commun accord entre un employé et son responsable.

Additional Information

GE Vernova offers a great work environment, professional development, challenging careers, and competitive compensation. GE Vernova is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law.

GE Vernova will only employ those who are legally authorized to work in the United States for this opening. Any offer of employment is conditioned upon the successful completion of a drug screen (as applicable).

Relocation Assistance Provided:
No

This is a remote position

For candidates applying to a U.S. based position, the pay range for this position is between $114,100.00 and $190,200.00. The Company pays a geographic differential of 110%, 120% or 130% of salary in certain areas. jobs.title: Project Manager, Patient Safety - Remote, Canada
jobs.description:
Project Safety Lead, Product Safety Services (PSS)

Lead global drug safety projects, manage your own project portfolio and be the trusted safety partner our sponsors rely on. In this role you will oversee adverse event processing, expedited reporting and quality, delivering compliant, on-time results for clients and regulators worldwide.

This role is for upcoming future opportunities that may arise at Fortrea

Key Responsibilities

Lead and manage global or regional safety projects, harmonising communications and processes.
Oversee adverse event processing from any source, including data entry, MedDRA coding, narratives, expectedness assessment and medical review.
Oversee expedited safety reports (ESRs), including triage, quality review, EudraVigilance activities and on-time submission to clients and regulators.
Perform or oversee quality review, signal detection, trend recognition and aggregate reporting.
Prepare Safety Management Plans, reconciliation plans and monthly status reports.
Monitor deliverables against contract assumptions, flag out-of-scope work and contribute to time and cost estimates.
Act as the sponsor-facing safety lead in client meetings, audits and safety committees (including DSMBs).
Train, mentor and support colleagues, and contribute to SOPs and work instructions.
Other duties as needed or assigned.

Required Qualifications

Education and safety experience (minimum), one of:

Non-degree plus 6–7 years' safety experience
Associate degree (including RN) plus 5–6 years' safety experience
BS/BA plus 4–5 years' safety experience
MS/MA plus 2–3 years' safety experience (or 3–4 years' relevant experience)
PharmD plus 1–2 years' safety experience (or 2–3 years' relevant experience)
Degrees in Biological Sciences, Pharmacy, Nursing, Life Sciences or Chemistry are preferred. Equivalent experience may be considered in lieu of education requirements.

In Addition, All Candidates Must Have

2+ years of project management experience.

Essential Skills And Experience

Significant experience leading safety projects and independently managing a portfolio of projects.
Strong project management and safety leadership, overseeing delivery, priorities, risks and competing demands across projects.
Significant clinical trial safety experience and a sound understanding of pharmacovigilance requirements.
Strong client and sponsor-facing skills: listening carefully, understanding sponsor needs and giving clear, pragmatic guidance and strategic direction.
Excellent written, verbal and presentation skills, with strong negotiation and stakeholder management.
Proven ability to collaborate across functions with internal and external stakeholders.
Strong budget and financial management, including oversight of deliverables against contractual assumptions and spotting out-of-scope work or budget risk.
Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills, anticipating issues, evaluating options and supporting decisions.
Excellent organisation and attention to detail, with a strategic view of project and portfolio priorities.
Good knowledge of worldwide pharmacovigilance regulations, GCP and ICH guidelines.

Nice To Have

Post-marketing safety experience in addition to clinical trial safety.
Experience supporting complex global or regional safety portfolios.
Exposure to aggregate reporting, risk management and broader pharmacovigilance.
Experience mentoring less-experienced colleagues.
EudraVigilance certification and knowledge of Medical Device Reporting.

Physical Demands / Work Environment

Office environment.
Travel of 10–15%, including overnight stays as project needs and office location require.

What We Offer

Be at the forefront of drug safety and clinical research in a global, growth-focused organisation.
Work with talented professionals and senior leaders to shape the future of clinical research.
Enjoy a collaborative culture, competitive benefits and opportunities for professional growth.

Candidates must be legally authorized to work in Canada. Fortrea is unable to provide visa or work permit sponsorship of any kind for this position.

Pay Range:
CAD 105,000-123,000

Benefits:
All job offers will be based on a candidate's skills and prior relevant experience, applicable degrees/certifications, as well as internal equity and market data. Regular, full-time or part-time employees working 20 or more hours per week are eligible for comprehensive benefits including: Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, STD/LTD, 401(k), Paid time off (PTO) or Flexible time off (FTO), Company bonus where applicable.

Application Deadline:
11/11/26

jobs.title: Project Manager (Remote)
jobs.description:
Req198143

Position Purpose

The Project Manager is responsible for a combination of planning and execution of activities related to delivery of projects and/or financial/budgeting activity for their teams. When executing on project delivery, Project Managers are responsible for the success of one or more projects within a given timeline and budget, creation and maintenance of status reports, proactively managing issues and risks, and can work with 3rd party partners. When performing financial/budgeting activities they monitor and adjust to given budgets, track labor, capital spend, and support variance root cause analysis.

Key Responsibilities

75% - Delivery & Execution - Establishes and executes effective communication with Project Stakeholders; Partners with stakeholders to lead the project planning effort, including the formulation of the project scope, definition of the project deliverables and the required delivery dates, creation of a logical work breakdown structure, and definition of major project milestones; Understands organizational/initiative goals and success criteria to apply to project work. Ability and understanding of project plans and development, risk identification & mitigation. Applies lessons learned to inform future initiatives; Creates, monitors, tracks, and adjusts project plans based on critical milestones for a project of group of initiatives; Assists in development, then executes change management process and activities within Technology organization; Works with stakeholders to determine and align dependencies, then proactively risk and issues via identification and mitigation plans.
25% - Resource & Financial Management - Executes fiscal management and reporting for operational, product/business, technology, and vendor stakeholders; includes gross labor, capital spend, and non-labor forecasting for tracking, reporting, and variance analysis.

Direct Manager/Direct Reports

Position Reports to Senior Director, Pro Paint.
Position has 0 direct reports.

Travel Requirements

Typically requires overnight travel 5% to 20% of the time.

Physical Requirements

Most of the time is spent sitting in a comfortable position and there is frequent opportunity to move about. On rare occasions, there may be a need to move or lift light articles.

Working Conditions

Located in a comfortable indoor area. Any unpleasant conditions would be infrequent and not objectionable.

Minimum Qualifications

Must be eighteen years of age or older.
Must be legally permitted to work in the United States.
Proficient knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite.
Proficient knowledge of Tableau.
Demonstrated ability to collaborate and work effectively with cross-functional teams.
Ability to draw accurate conclusions from financial documentation.
Demonstrated project management skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Experience with the planning and execution of projects and risk mitigation strategies.
Experience with project management execution in a modern software environment; experience managing technical projects.
Proficient knowledge of GBQ.
Experience in Agile, Waterfall or other project delivery methodologies.

Preferred Qualifications

Project/program management experience leading multiple technology, AI, automation, or emerging-technology initiatives simultaneously.
Proven ability to manage roadmaps, milestones, timelines, risks, dependencies, and deliverables across complex projects.
Strong cross-functional leadership, partnering with engineering, AI/ML, ServiceNow, cybersecurity, telephony, operations, and business teams.
Ability to translate between technical and business teams, clarify priorities, and drive execution when requirements evolve.
Strong stakeholder communication and executive-level reporting, including project status, risks, decisions, and escalations.
Experience driving technology adoption and organizational change from planning through implementation.
Familiarity with AI/ML, Microsoft Copilot/Copilot Studio, ServiceNow, conversational AI, contact-center technology, or similar automation platforms.
Experience in contact-center, IT support, or Technology Support Center environments, with an understanding of operational outcomes such as productivity, first-contact resolution, and cost per ticket.

Minimum Education

The knowledge, skills and abilities typically acquired through the completion of a bachelor's degree program or equivalent degree in a field of study related to the job.

Preferred Education

No additional education.

Minimum Years Of Work Experience

2

Preferred Years Of Work Experience

No additional years of experience

Minimum Leadership Experience

No previous leadership experience

Preferred Leadership Experience

2+ years of previous leadership experience

Certifications

PMP Certified

Competencies

Manages Ambiguity
Collaborates
Optimizes Work Processes
Plans and Aligns
Communicates Effectively
Drives Results
Financial Acumen

jobs.title: Project Manager
jobs.description:
At Associated Bank we strive to create an inclusive culture where different perspectives are valued and recognized as strengths critical to our success. If you thrive in an environment where your growth and development are encouraged and supported, then Associated Bank may be the right place for you.

Associated Bank requires you to directly represent yourself and your own experiences during the recruiting and hiring process. Associated Bank conducts a thorough background check on all new hires.

Role Summary

The Project Manager is responsible for leading and coordinating small to medium-sized business projects while ensuring successful execution throughout the project lifecycle. This role serves as a key liaison among business partners, leadership, project teams, and third-party vendors, driving projects to completion while balancing scope, timeline, cost, and quality. The Project Manager continues to build expertise in project management and develops a deeper understanding of the business areas they support.

Key Accountabilities

Lead cross-functional teams in the successful execution and implementation of business projects.
Develop and maintain project plans, timelines, and status reporting to ensure projects remain on track and stakeholders stay informed.
Identify, assess, and address project risks, issues, and changing requirements to support successful outcomes.
Manage project scope, schedules, resources, and budgets to achieve project objectives.
Support all phases of the project lifecycle, including requirements gathering, testing, design reviews, change management, and production readiness activities.
Plan and coordinate multiple interrelated tasks and initiatives based on business value, scope, schedule, and resource requirements.
Conduct research and analysis to define requirements, evaluate feasibility, and support high-quality project execution.
Partner with vendors and third parties throughout selection, contract review, and project delivery processes.

Required

Education & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Business or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
2-4 years of experience in banking, business, or project management.
Knowledge and exposure to fundamental project management theories, principles, and concepts.
Demonstrated ability to manage projects, prioritize competing demands, and adapt to changing business needs.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.

Why You’ll Love Working Here

This role offers the opportunity to work on meaningful business initiatives while developing your project management expertise and expanding your organizational knowledge. You'll collaborate with cross-functional teams, build strong business relationships, and contribute to projects that drive business success.

Apply today to make an impact.

We welcome and encourage applications from all qualified parties, including but not limited to people returning to the workforce, people with disabilities, those without a college degree, and veterans or those with military experience.

In addition to core traditional benefits, we take pride in offering benefits for every stage of life.

Retirement savings including both 401(k) and Pension plans.
Paid time off to volunteer in your community.
Opportunities to connect with others through our diversity-focused Colleague Resource Groups.
Competitive salaries with professional development and advancement opportunities.
Bonus benefits including well-being programs and incentives, parental leave, an employee stock purchase plan, military benefits and much more.
Personal banking, loan, investment and insurance benefits.

Associated Bank serves more than 120 communities throughout Wisconsin, Illinois, Minnesota, and Missouri and we consider our colleagues critical to our continued success. See why our colleagues continually vote us a best place to work in the Midwest. Join our community on Facebook, LinkedIn and X.

To support our recruiting process, we may use artificial intelligence ("AI") or automated technologies to collect, organize, sort, and analyze information submitted by applicants. These tools may assist our Talent Acquisition professionals in identifying applicants who appear to satisfy the minimum qualifications for a position.

AI is not used to make employment decisions on behalf of Associated Bank. No applicant will be selected or rejected solely based on the output of an AI tool. Hiring decisions are made by Associated Bank personnel who review applicant information and exercise independent judgment in accordance with applicable law and company policies.

Compliance Statement

Associated Bank is an equal opportunity employer committed to creating a diverse workforce. We support a work environment where colleagues are respected and given the opportunity to perform to their fullest potential. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, religion, color, sex, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or veteran status, among other factors.

Fully complies with all applicable enterprise policies and procedures. Acts in compliance with all applicable laws and regulations as outlined in training materials, including but not limited to Bank Secrecy Act. Responsible for reporting suspicious activity to Financial Intelligence. Responsible to report all customer complaints as prescribed and procedure violations to management or HR.

Responsible to report ethical concerns as needed to Associated Bank’s anonymous Ethics Hotline.

Associated Bank provides additional assistance throughout the application, interview and hiring process. Please contact leavesandaccommodations@associatedbank.com if you need an accommodation at any time during the process.

Associated Banc-Corp participates in the E-Verify Program. E-Verify Notice English or Spanish. Know Your Right to Work English or Spanish.

jobs.title: Technical Consulting Senior Project Manager
jobs.description:
Job Description:

Technical Consulting Principal Project Manager

The Broadcom Mainframe Software Division (MSD) is looking for a Principal level IT Technical Project Manager to direct complex, high-stake cross functional software migration and related projects, typically overseeing portfolios related to program level engagements.

This role is related to MSD Technical Consulting Services billable engagements for large, diverse Fortune 500 companies. The Principal Project Manager defines governance and strategy, identifies and manages stakeholders, creates formal kickoff deliverables, builds project schedules, manages budgets, risks and issues provides expert leadership with a proven track record of successful execution managing mainframe software projects.

Ability to measure projects and independently drive execution and own responsibility for overall success of projects with experience documenting projects as reference/success stories. Accomplished project delivery is the key performance metric for this role.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Direction & Leadership: Driving large-scale, complex projects from inception to implementation, ensuring alignment with company goals.
Project Governance: Creating and implementing project policies, procedures, and quality control standards.
Financial & Risk Management: Establishing budgets, controlling costs, forecasting expenditures, and managing risk mitigation strategies.
Stakeholder Management: Communicating project status, risks, and ROI to executive leadership, while managing relationships with clients and internal partners.
Process Improvement: Analyzing operational efficiency and developing solutions, to streamline workflows.
Team Leadership: Mentoring and guiding project teams, delegating tasks, and managing Broadcom and customer project resources.

Required Skills And Qualifications

Experience: Bachelors in business, engineering, or a related field; certifications like PMP (Project Management Professional) are often preferred or 8+ years of related experience or Masters degree and 6+ years of related experience
Requires 6+ years of project management experience, often with a focus on cross-functional, large-scale projects.
1-3+ years of Mainframe Software project management experience required.
Technical Proficiency: Advanced knowledge of project management tools, databases, and Microsoft Office (Excel, PowerPoint, MS Project).
Leadership/Soft Skills: Excellent communication, strategic thinking, negotiation, and conflict resolution skills.

Certification: PMP Certification or equivalent experience is preferred.

Compensation And Benefits

The annual base salary range for this position is USD 100,000.00 To USD 160,000.00

As a valued member of our team, you'll be eligible for a discretionary annual bonus and the opportunity to receive not only a competitive new hire equity grant, but also annual equity awards, connecting your success directly to the company's growth. All subject to relevant plan documents and award agreements.

Broadcom offers a competitive and comprehensive benefits package: Medical, dental and vision plans, 401(K) participation including company matching, Employee Stock Purchase Program (ESPP), Employee Assistance Program (EAP), company paid holidays, paid sick leave and vacation time. The company follows all applicable laws for Paid Family Leave and other leaves of absence.

Lead global drug safety projects, manage your own project portfolio and be the trusted safety partner our sponsors rely on. In this role you will oversee adverse event processing, expedited reporting and quality, delivering compliant, on-time results for clients and regulators worldwide.

Lead and manage global or regional safety projects, harmonising communications and processes.
Oversee adverse event processing from any source, including data entry, MedDRA coding, narratives, expectedness assessment and medical review.
Oversee expedited safety reports (ESRs), including triage, quality review, EudraVigilance activities and on-time submission to clients and regulators.
Perform or oversee quality review, signal detection, trend recognition and aggregate reporting.
Prepare Safety Management Plans, reconciliation plans and monthly status reports.
Monitor deliverables against contract assumptions, flag out-of-scope work and contribute to time and cost estimates.
Act as the sponsor-facing safety lead in client meetings, audits and safety committees (including DSMBs).
Train, mentor and support colleagues, and contribute to SOPs and work instructions.

Required Qualifications

Education and safety experience (minimum), one of:

Non-degree plus 6–7 years' safety experience
Associate degree (including RN) plus 5–6 years' safety experience
BS/BA plus 4–5 years' safety experience
MS/MA plus 2–3 years' safety experience (or 3–4 years' relevant experience)
PharmD plus 1–2 years' safety experience (or 2–3 years' relevant experience)
Degrees in Biological Sciences, Pharmacy, Nursing, Life Sciences or Chemistry are preferred. Equivalent experience may be considered in lieu of education requirements.

2+ years of project management experience.

Essential Skills And Experience

Significant experience leading safety projects and independently managing a portfolio of projects.
Strong project management and safety leadership, overseeing delivery, priorities, risks and competing demands across projects.
Significant clinical trial safety experience and a sound understanding of pharmacovigilance requirements.
Strong client and sponsor-facing skills: listening carefully, understanding sponsor needs and giving clear, pragmatic guidance and strategic direction.
Excellent written, verbal and presentation skills, with strong negotiation and stakeholder management.
Proven ability to collaborate across functions with internal and external stakeholders.
Strong budget and financial management, including oversight of deliverables against contractual assumptions and spotting out-of-scope work or budget risk.
Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills, anticipating issues, evaluating options and supporting decisions.

Post-marketing safety experience in addition to clinical trial safety.
Experience supporting complex global or regional safety portfolios.

EudraVigilance certification and knowledge of Medical Device Reporting.

Office environment.
Travel of 10–15%, including overnight stays as project needs and office location require.

Be at the forefront of drug safety and clinical research in a global, growth-focused organisation.

jobs.title: Project Manager – Technical and Field Operations
jobs.description:
About Draganfly

Draganfly Inc. (the “Company”) has been a recognized technology leader within the commercial UAV space for over two decades. We helped establish the commercial market & adoption of multi-rotor helicopters for public safety, agriculture, aerial imaging, & more. As a leader who helped shape the industry, Draganfly’s focus is on the sale of drone products and services, contract engineering & custom integration product development, and health monitoring products and services.

Additional information on our expertise, projects, and culture can be found at https://draganfly.com/

Draganfly is seeking a Project Manager to lead the planning and execution of customer-facing, technical, and cross-functional projects across the organization. This role will serve as a primary point of coordination between customers, Engineering, Operations, Sales, Field Operations, Logistics, and other internal stakeholders to ensure projects are clearly defined, properly resourced, effectively managed, and successfully delivered.

The ideal candidate is an experienced project manager with the technical aptitude to work effectively alongside engineering and technical teams without needing to serve as the subject matter expert. This individual will manage multiple concurrent projects, communicate directly with customers and partners, coordinate cross-functional teams, and maintain strong execution throughout the project lifecycle. This role reports directly to the PMO Lead and works closely with Program Managers, functional leaders, technical teams, subject-matter experts, cross-functional teams, and Project Coordinators.

Key Responsibilities

Project Leadership & Delivery

Lead assigned customer-facing, technical, integration, special, and cross-functional projects from initiation through delivery and closeout.
Establish and maintain project objectives, scope, schedules, milestones, risks, dependencies, stakeholders, and acceptance criteria.
Develop project plans aligned with the complexity, risk, and delivery requirements of each initiative.
Maintain accountability for assigned projects while coordinating work across multiple functional teams.
Monitor project progress, resource requirements, schedules, and deliverables to support successful execution.
Identify and address project risks, constraints, schedule impacts, and resource requirements in collaboration with the appropriate stakeholders.
Manage multiple concurrent projects while maintaining clear priorities and consistent stakeholder communication.
Support internal Engineering projects as portfolio capacity permits.

Customer & Stakeholder Management

Serve as the primary project-management point of contact for assigned customers, partners, and external stakeholders.
Facilitate customer and technical meetings to define requirements, integration needs, delivery expectations, and acceptance criteria.
Translate technical project progress into clear customer-facing updates while enabling Engineering personnel to remain focused on technical execution.
Coordinate with Engineering and technical subject matter experts to obtain accurate information and resolve customer questions.
Communicate project updates, changes, decisions, and milestones professionally and transparently.
Maintain strong relationships with customers and internal stakeholders throughout the project lifecycle.

Cross-Functional Coordination

Coordinate project activities across Engineering, Operations, Field Operations, Sales/Business Development, Logistics, Procurement, and other functional teams.
Establish clear ownership of project deliverables, actions, dependencies, and handoffs.
Facilitate internal project meetings to review progress, priorities, risks, and upcoming milestones.
Coordinate technical requirements between customers and internal teams while supporting efficient use of technical resources.
Ensure appropriate stakeholders are engaged at each stage of the project lifecycle.
Support the execution of special initiatives that span multiple organizational functions.

Demo, Training & Event Oversight

Maintain project-level accountability for assigned demonstrations, customer trainings, trade shows, and operational events.
Coordinate personnel, equipment, logistics, customer requirements, and readiness activities leading up to execution.
Partner with Project Coordinators to ensure event intake, scheduling, calendar management, readiness tracking, logistics follow-up, and administrative requirements are completed.
Monitor project readiness, customer requirements, schedule alignment, and operational planning.
Support pre-event and customer planning activities as required.

Who Are You Really?

You are a highly organized project leader who can manage multiple priorities, stakeholders, and workstreams in a fast-paced environment.
You communicate clearly and professionally with customers, partners, technical teams, and senior stakeholders.
You take ownership, exercise sound judgment, follow through on commitments, and solve problems proactively.
You can influence and coordinate cross-functional contributors who do not directly report to you.
You have the technical aptitude to understand discussions, identify requirements and risks, and drive follow-up actions without needing to be the subject matter expert.
You are comfortable balancing customer expectations with technical, operational, resource, and schedule constraints.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in project management, business administration, engineering, operations, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
Demonstrated experience managing projects involving multiple stakeholders, functional teams, or workstreams.
Strong project-management fundamentals, including scope, schedule, risk, dependency, stakeholder, and issue management.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Demonstrated ability to communicate professionally with customers and external stakeholders.
Ability to organize and manage multiple concurrent priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Strong judgment, ownership, follow-through, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to influence and coordinate personnel who do not directly report to the Project Manager.
Ability to understand technical discussions sufficiently to identify requirements, dependencies, risks, and follow-up actions.
Comfortable using project-management and collaboration software.
Ability and willingness to travel as required in support of customer engagements, project execution, demonstrations, integrations, validation activities, and other business needs.

Preferred Qualifications & Certifications

PMP certification or demonstrated progress toward PMP certification.
Experience working in aerospace, unmanned aircraft systems (UAS), robotics, engineering, or another technical environment.
Experience managing technical integration, product-development, or customer-delivery projects.
Experience working directly with engineers and technical subject matter experts.
Experience supporting government, military, public-safety, or enterprise customers.
Experience using ClickUp or a comparable project-management platform.
General technical aptitude across mechanical, electrical, software, communications, aviation, or related technology areas.

Compensation Package

Competitive salary: $80,000–$100,000 USD
Health Coverage Reimbursement: We reimburse the cost of your existing or preferred healthcare plan (amount varies depending on family size).
401(k) program with employer matching
Generous time-off program, including vacation, wellness days, and the week off between Christmas and New Year’s.
Professional development support, including assistance in obtaining or maintaining role-relevant certifications (e.g., PMP certification, where applicable).

Why Join Us?

At Draganfly Innovations, you’ll join a collaborative team that values innovation, curiosity, and continuous improvement. We’re in an exciting growth phase, scaling our technologies, product lines, and teams as we continue to shape the future of UAV innovation. Joining us now means becoming part of a company with deep roots in the industry - and bold ambitions for what comes next.

You’ll have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact, work on diverse and cutting‑edge projects, and grow your skills alongside passionate experts. We offer competitive compensation, strong benefits, and a supportive environment where your contributions truly matter. Here, you won’t just join a company - you’ll help build what comes next. As part of our hiring process, all candidates must successfully complete reference checks and a criminal background check.

You will help customers turn transformation goals into clear execution plans by bringing structure, visibility, and accountability across interconnected projects. Lead delivery of multi-workstream professional services engagements for large and strategic customers

Proven ability to build collaborative relationships with customers and partner effectively with Engagement Managers, Architects, and delivery teams
Working knowledge of agile and other project management approaches, with the judgment to apply the right structure to different customer needs
Ability to develop long-term plans that support customer adoption, transformation, and successful delivery outcomes
Comfort leading program-level meetings and driving progress across multiple workstreams
Willingness to complete GitLab Project Management certification within 2 months of starting in the role

On our Professional Services team, we help customers adopt GitLab effectively by turning strategy into structured delivery. As Program Managers on our team, we bring clarity to large, complex engagements by coordinating people, plans, and processes across multiple workstreams. We work closely with customers, Engagement Managers, Architects, and delivery leaders to create practical plans, manage risk, and keep programs moving toward agreed outcomes. Because we operate in an all-remote, asynchronous environment, we value clear communication, strong documentation, and ownership. This role is well suited for you if you enjoy building order in complex environments, guiding stakeholders through change, and helping customers make progress on meaningful transformation efforts.

jobs.description:
About The Company

Valon is the leading AI platform for mortgage servicing, building the AI-native operating system for regulated finance.

Before providing the system of record that powers the entire industry, we built and ran our own mortgage servicer on it. That gave us a real regulated environment to prove our technology could replace the mainframe systems servicers have used for decades. Carrington acquired that servicer and adopted ValonOS as its core platform, allowing us to focus entirely on scaling our SaaS platform.

ValonOS is now on track to power 1 in 6 U.S. mortgages across major mortgage servicers like Newrez, Carrington, and ServiceMac. Every process on the platform is structured and programmable, enabling our AI agents to perform core servicing work, like handling payments, escrow, and homeowner questions, directly within the system's controls.

We recently raised a $150 million Series D at a $2.3 billion valuation by new investor Ribbit Capital, with continued support from existing backer a16z, amongst others.

About The Role

Valon is rebuilding the mortgage servicing industry from the ground up . We're looking for a Technical Program Manager (TPM)
to join our team and help us launch complex products that will revolutionize how mortgage servicers operate. This is an exciting opportunity to shape the future of our TPM function and make a significant impact on our product development process.

In this role, you'll be instrumental in coordinating efforts across multiple engineering teams, ensuring seamless communication, and driving the successful delivery of our most critical initiatives. If you're a seasoned TPM with a passion for tackling challenging problems and a desire to build a function from the ground up, we encourage you to apply.

What You'll Do

Lead End-to-End Program Management: Own the planning, execution, and delivery of complex technical programs from conception through launch, including defining scope, setting timelines, and managing risks.
Drive Cross-Functional Coordination: Facilitate effective communication and collaboration between multiple engineering teams, product managers, design, operations, and other stakeholders to ensure alignment and shared understanding.
Optimize Development Processes: Identify and implement process improvements to enhance efficiency, predictability, and quality across the product development lifecycle.
Manage Stakeholder Expectations: Proactively communicate program status, risks, and dependencies to all relevant stakeholders, ensuring transparency and alignment.
Mitigate Risks and Resolve Issues: Identify potential roadblocks and actively work to resolve technical, operational, and organizational challenges that may impact program delivery.
Define and Track Metrics: Establish clear success metrics for programs and regularly track progress, providing data-driven insights to inform decision-making.
Contribute to Team Growth: As our second TPM, you'll have a unique opportunity to help define the vision, strategy, and best practices for the TPM function at Valon.

What You'll Bring

5+ years of experience as a Technical Program Manager in a fast-paced, complex software development environment.
Proven track record of successfully delivering large-scale, cross-functional technical programs.
Strong understanding of the software development lifecycle (SDLC) and various agile methodologies.
Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence and align diverse stakeholders.
Excellent problem-solving abilities and a proactive approach to identifying and mitigating risks.
Ability to thrive in a dynamic, rapidly evolving startup environment.
Prior experience in fintech team is a plus, but not required.

Description

Archaeology Project/Program Manager

Portland, Seattle, or Pacific Northwes
t

ICF is seeking a senior archaeologist to help plan, monitor, and manage cultural resources projects and programs in the Pacific Northwest and the western Unites States. As an Archaeology Project/Program Manager at ICF you will help deliver and continue to grow our Cultural Resources Management (CRM) services for existing clients. The Archaeology Project/Program Manager will also partner with other environmental program managers to expand ICF’s business, and with other CRM leaders across geographies to expand the CRM practice.

This position is intended to be based in either our Portland, OR or Seattle, WA office, however it can be fully or partially remote, and applicants living throughout the region are encouraged to apply. The Archaeology Project/Program Manager should be comfortable working across the primary disciplines that comprise cultural resources management (archaeology, built environment, tribal resources, landscapes) and comfortably navigate between project management (scoping, staffing, progress reporting) and delivery of technical services (quality control, schedule, cost). You will combine your archaeology technical skills with strong regulatory compliance expertise to develop project-level analysis and programmatic solutions for SEPA, NEPA, and Section 106 reviews. You will also be expected to contribute to marketing and proposal efforts for cultural resources opportunities or as part of a larger team on multi-disciplinary opportunities.

Our Environment and Planning division provides a range of consulting services in environmental analysis and compliance (e.g., NEPA) for clients in the transportation, water, energy, and natural resources sectors. Our clients include federal, state and local agencies, and private energy and utility companies. At ICF we combine passion for our work with industry expertise and innovative analytics to produce compelling results throughout the entire program life cycle, from research and analysis through implementation and improvement.

Although the range below is wider to accommodate growth within the job, this position will have a starting pay range of $110,000 to $130,000 based on % match of qualifications/experience/responsibilities, location, and other.

Key Responsibilities

Serve as a project or task manager on large or complex cultural resources and environmental planning projects.
Provide analysis for environmental regulatory reviews under SEPA, NEPA, and Section 106 and compose defensible arguments and supporting documentation.
Interface directly with key clients and help build and maintain great relationships.
Contribute to identifying new project leads, developing pursuit strategies, and writing proposals.
Exercise judgment in selecting methods, techniques and quality assurance for deliverables.
Supervise and/or mentor less experienced staff as they grow their technical, business development, and client relations capabilities.

Required Skills/Experience

Masters degree in anthropology or related field.
10+ years of CRM and/or environmental planning experience within the energy, water, transportation, and/or Federal Agency markets.
Experience obtaining concurrence for SEPA and NHPA Section 106 findings, reviewing technical studies such as those addressing archaeology, architectural history, historic landscapes, consistency with Secretary of the Interior Standards for the Treatment of Historic Properties, effects analysis, and mitigation strategies.
Must either already be approved as an Oregon Qualified Archaeologist, or have the qualifications and experience to be approved as such by the State of Oregon.

Preferred Skills/Experience

Strong work ethic with a positive attitude and thrives in a team-oriented setting.
Advanced knowledge and understanding of environmental planning, cultural resources management and regulatory compliance with SEPA, NEPA, NHPA, and other state and federal environmental regulations.
Familiarity with Oregon and Washington resources and associated regulatory environment.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills with experience interfacing with external clients, members of the general public, and government officials.
Strong analytical skills, including attention to detail, as well as technical writing and communication skills.
Strong project management skills, including ability to take and give direction, stay organized, and manage time effectively.
Commitment to overseeing preparation of high-quality work within established budgets and schedules.

ICF is a global advisory and technology services provider, but we’re not your typical consultants. We combine unmatched expertise with cutting-edge technology to help clients solve their most complex challenges, navigate change, and shape the future.

We can only solve the world's toughest challenges by building a workplace that allows everyone to thrive. We are an equal opportunity employer. jobs.description:
Description

Amazon FSx provides fully managed, high-performance file storage that powers some of the most critical workloads running on AWS today, from GPU-heavy AI/ML training to high-performance computing (HPC) and enterprise applications. We are looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager to own end-to-end delivery of programs that span multiple FSx engineering teams and partner organizations across AWS and other companies.

In this role, you will turn ambiguous, multi-quarter goals into plans with clear milestones, owners, and critical paths, then drive them to launch. You will go deep enough technically to challenge designs, broker trade-offs between teams, and recognize when a plan is off track before the schedule says so. This is not a status-reporting role. If you are a collaborative problem-solver who thrives on bringing order to complexity at cloud scale.

Key job responsibilities

Own the integrated plan for cross-team FSx programs, including scope, schedule, dependencies, risks, and critical path, from concept through general availability and regional expansion.
Partner with product managers, principal engineers, and software development managers to define and sequence the FSx technical roadmap, making explicit trade-offs between scope, date, and quality.
Manage dependencies on partner teams across AWS (EC2, networking, S3, EBS, identity, and infrastructure) and external companies.
Define and track the KPIs that matter for a storage service, such as launch predictability, capacity headroom, availability, latency, and operational load, and use them to drive durable improvements.
Drive operational excellence and automation programs that reduce undifferentiated work, including adoption of generative AI tooling across engineering teams, and communicate progress through crisp written narratives to Directors and VPs.

A day in the life

You start your morning reviewing service and program metrics for the FSx launches you own. By mid-morning, you are running a cross-functional alignment meeting with engineers and product managers, driving crisp decisions on competing priorities and surfacing risks early. After lunch, you join a technical design review where you pressure-test assumptions and help the team navigate a key architectural trade-off. Later, you draft a program update for senior AWS leadership, translating complex dependencies into clear recommendations and next steps.

About The Team

Amazon FSx is an AWS storage service launched in 2018 that delivers fully managed file systems for customers running AI/ML, HPC, and enterprise workloads at scale. Our team operates with the pace and autonomy of a startup inside AWS, directly accountable for customer satisfaction, service reliability, and innovation. You will work alongside product managers, principal engineers, and software development managers who are passionate about building cloud storage that customers depend on. We are focused on growing the service's capabilities and reach, and we value an inclusive environment where every team member can contribute and do their best work.

7+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience

Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules

5+ years of project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management experience
Experience managing projects across cross functional teams, building sustainable processes and coordinating release schedules
Experience defining KPI's/SLA's used to drive multi-million dollar businesses and reporting to senior leadership

jobs.title: Staff Technical Program Manager, IT Audit & Governance
jobs.description:
We're looking for a senior, hands-on leader to own IT audit and governance across all of our applications, infrastructure, and systems. You'll be accountable for keeping IT audit-ready every day: SOX ITGCs and ITACs, plus the broader audit and governance obligations that touch the technology stack (SOC reports, ISO, security and regulatory audits).

This role is about accountability and execution. You'll work with cross-functional IT leaders across Infrastructure, Engineering, Security, Cloud, Enterprise Applications, and Business Systems to make sure controls are owned, operated, evidenced, and remediated on time. You'll also be the primary IT liaison to Internal Audit, Finance/SOX PMO, and external auditors. You operate independently, influence without authority, and can speak credibly with an engineer about a CI/CD pipeline and with the CAO about a deficiency.

We're looking to speak with candidates based in Palo Alto or New York City for our hybrid working model.

What You'll Do

Own audit and governance across all IT

Own the audit and governance program across all IT applications, infrastructure, cloud platforms, and supporting systems
Maintain a complete inventory of systems, owners, and applicable audit and compliance obligations (SOX, SOC 1/SOC 2, ISO 27001, and other regulatory or customer requirements)
Build and run an IT audit calendar that coordinates SOX, internal audit, external audit, and compliance activities to reduce duplicate asks and audit fatigue
Establish governance standards, policies, and control frameworks that apply consistently across IT

Drive accountability and execution with IT leaders

Partner with cross-functional IT leaders to assign clear control and remediation ownership, with defined deadlines and escalation paths
Run regular governance forums and control health reviews with IT leadership, reporting status, risks, and overdue items
Hold teams accountable for timely control execution, evidence quality, and issue closure, escalating early when commitments slip
Translate audit and compliance requirements into practical work that engineering and infrastructure teams can adopt without slowing delivery

Own ITGC and ITAC compliance

Own the end-to-end SOX IT program: scoping inputs, control design, ownership, evidence, readiness testing, and issue management
Maintain the ITGC framework (access management, change management, IT operations, SDLC) across all in-scope applications, databases, operating systems, and cloud infrastructure
Own ITAC strategy and coverage with Finance and business-system owners: automated controls, configurations, interfaces, calculations, and approval workflows
Own IPE/report validation, ITAC baselines, and segregation of duties (SoD) across ERP and key financial applications

Design, operate, and strengthen controls

Design controls that are engineered into IT workflows (ticketing, CI/CD, IAM, CMDB) rather than layered on manually
Run readiness and self-assessment testing ahead of Internal Audit and external auditor testing
Rationalize overlapping controls across frameworks so one control and one piece of evidence can satisfy multiple requirements
Drive automation and continuous control monitoring to reduce manual effort and audit burden
Manage SOC 1/SOC 2 report reviews, CUECs, and third-party/vendor control dependencies

Drive remediation and issue management

Own the issue lifecycle across IT, from identification and root cause through remediation plan, validation, and closure
Prepare management's response to audit findings and provide the IT perspective on deficiency severity with Finance, Legal, and Internal Audit
Report control health and remediation status to IT leadership, the CAO, and the Audit Committee as needed

Be the IT face to auditors and the business

Serve as primary IT contact for Internal Audit and external auditors on scope, walkthroughs, evidence requests, and reliance strategy
Coordinate PBC requests, evidence standards, and timelines across IT teams
Train and enable control owners and IT leaders on audit requirements, evidence quality, and their responsibilities

Lead and elevate the program

Set standards for control documentation, evidence, and issue management across IT
Mentor analysts and guide co-source or outsourced resources
Contribute to emerging governance areas such as AI/emerging technology

What You'll Bring

Required

8-12+ years of experience in IT audit, SOX compliance, IT governance, or technology risk (Big 4, internal audit, or in-house IT GRC)
Deep, hands-on experience with SOX 404 ITGCs and ITACs in a public company
Working knowledge of COSO, COBIT, and PCAOB AS 2201, and how external auditors approach IT reliance and ITAC testing
Experience across modern technology environments: cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP), SaaS, ERP (e.g., Oracle, NetSuite, SAP), infrastructure, and identity/access platforms
Familiarity with other frameworks and audits (SOC 1/SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST) and how to harmonize them
Proven track record of owning programs end-to-end and driving accountability and execution across multiple teams and senior leaders without direct authority
Excellent communication and executive presence, including negotiating with auditors and briefing senior leadership
Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Accounting, Computer Science, or a related field

Preferred

CISA, CISSP, CIA, CPA, or equivalent certification
Experience with GRC and audit tools (e.g., AuditBoard, ServiceNow GRC, Workiva, Archer)
Data analytics skills (SQL, Python, Power BI/Tableau) for full-population testing and control monitoring
Experience in high-growth, SaaS, or technology company environments
Familiarity with DevOps/CI-CD, infrastructure-as-code, and change management in agile environments

What Success Looks Like

First 90 days: Map the IT landscape, systems, control owners, and audit obligations. Build relationships with IT leaders, Finance, Internal Audit, and external auditors. Identify the top gaps, ownership issues, and quick wins.
6 months: Stand up a governance cadence with IT leaders, with clear ownership and on-time execution. Complete a full readiness cycle with controls evidenced on time and no surprises from auditors.
12 months: Reduce control count and manual effort through rationalization and automation, close prior-year findings, and establish a scalable, IT-owned audit and governance program with a consolidated audit calendar and framework

jobs.description:
Job Description Summary

** NOTE A COVER LETTER IS REQUIRED FOR CONSIDERATION **

The Transportation Research Board (TRB), a division of the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine, provides leadership in transportation innovation through objective, evidence-based research and convenes experts from government, industry, and academia to address complex transportation challenges. Within TRB, the Cooperative Research Programs (CRP) are applied research programs—including the National Cooperative Highway Research Program (NCHRP), Transit Cooperative Research Program (TCRP), Airport Cooperative Research Program (ACRP), and others—that develop practical, implementable solutions to current and emerging transportation issues through stakeholder-driven research and collaboration.

The Senior Program Manager - Planning and Environment provides senior-level program management for a complex and diverse portfolio of cooperative transportation research projects. This role has no direct supervisory responsibilities and combines portfolio-level accountability with hands-on management of complex and high-visibility research projects.

Reporting to the Program Director, the Senior Program Manager exercises substantial independent judgment in managing and overseeing project portfolios, resolving complex issues, and engaging with volunteers, sponsors, research agencies, and stakeholders. The role is accountable for ensuring research quality, operational effectiveness, and timely delivery across multiple topic areas, while aligning project activities with division priorities.

Job Description

Transportation Disciplines

This role involves leading and facilitating research efforts in collaboration with expert panels across diverse transportation topics for Panning and Environment.

Responsibilities

Project Panel Meeting Planning & Support

Review panel nominations and coordinate the formation of project panels.
Facilitate project panel meetings, support panel chairs, and follow up with notes and action items from panel meetings.
Prepare materials, schedules, and documentation needed to support effective panel deliberations and project decisions.
Document panel input, decisions, and recommendations to support timely project implementation and follow-up.

Proposal Development & Research Agency Selection

Work with prospective proposers to resolve matters related to submission of acceptable proposals.
Evaluate research proposals for technical merit and participate in the process of selecting research agencies.
Support fair, objective, and well-documented proposal review and research agency selection processes.

Research Planning & Contract Coordination

Become thoroughly familiar with selected research plans and work with research agencies and project panels to develop detailed working plans to accomplish project objectives.
Work with administrative offices to provide information necessary for contract negotiation and execution.
Clarify project objectives, technical expectations, schedules, deliverables, and performance requirements with research agencies and project panels.

Contract & Project Management

Assemble and submit the complete contract package, including all required documents, in accordance with CRP processes.
Manage contracts by establishing clear project objectives and technical approaches for achieving project goals.
Visit research agencies, as appropriate, to become familiar with their organizations and facilities, monitor work, and assess progress against project schedules.
Review monthly, quarterly, and other progress reports needed for administration of the program.
Prepare compliance reports that document project progress and assess research agency performance and accomplishments.

Project Monitoring & Quality Review

Conduct site visits, as appropriate.
Make critical reviews of project progress and recommend improvements when needed.
Review all types of reports that emanate from research for clarity, completeness, adherence to CRP format, and fulfillment of the approved research plan.
Make recommendations as to the acceptability of research products and deliverables.

Research Interpretation, Publication & Dissemination

Interpret project findings with respect to applicability for improving transportation practices.
Prepare research results digests and other derivative products.
Prepare forewords for use in published reports.
Make presentations on research findings at technical meetings and other professional forums.

Coordination & Program Support

Coordinate with appropriate agencies and subject-matter experts within assigned subject areas to ensure projects benefit from available knowledge.
Provide staff support to NCHRP oversight committee, American Association of State Highway and Transportation Officials (AASHTO) and the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) in formulating the annual NCHRP research program by reviewing and evaluating problem statements submitted for research.
Work effectively with sponsors, volunteers, research agencies, administrative offices, and colleagues to support timely and high-quality delivery of NCHRP research.

Confidentiality:
Maintains confidentiality. Handles secure, privileged, sensitive, or confidential information with discretion and in accordance with organizational policies and procedures. Maintains strict confidence to prevent disclosure. Accesses such information strictly for work-related purposes, and ensures that it is securely stored, transmitted, and disposed of in compliance with organization guidelines. Ensures procedures are in place to safeguard confidentiality and prevent unauthorized disclosure. Provides ongoing training and guidance to team members to reinforce best practices in handling confidential information

Requirements

Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Knowledge of cooperative or committee-driven research programs and familiarity with transportation research sponsors and policy environments.
Understanding of the National Academies’ mission, structure, and culture.
Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage complex portfolios and competing priorities.
Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to effectively engage stakeholders at all levels.
Ability to manage funding-related matters and high-risk or complex research initiatives.
Ability to operate with substantial independence, sound judgment, and discretion in a complex organizational environment.
Ability to solve complex problems involving significant variety and to serve as a resource to others in resolving issues.
Ability to work effectively in team-based settings and build and sustain collaborative relationships across departments and stakeholder groups.
Ability to perform effectively in complex, high-impact environments with multiple priorities and demands.

Minimum Education/Training Requirements

Master’s degree in a discipline relevant to transportation, highways, public policy, research management, or a closely related field; or a bachelor’s degree in a relevant discipline with significant professional experience demonstrating advanced subject matter expertise, management of complex projects or programs, and independent research, analysis, or policy development responsibilities.

Minimum Experience

Six years of related professional experience. Demonstrated impact on the advancement of science, transportation practice, or policy through the successful completion of National Academies activities or equivalent outside activities and through effective dissemination of these activities.
Significant experience managing applied research projects or programs.

Required Licenses, Certification or Registration: None

Any qualification to be considered equivalent, in lieu of stated minimum, requires the prior approval of the Office of Human Resources.

Other Details

Supervisory Responsibilities/Controls

Reports to the Program Director. Independently establishes goals and objectives. This position has no direct supervisory responsibilities.

Mental And Physical Capabilities

Ability to be visible on camera for meetings when remote.
Ability to use a computer and applicable hardware/software to perform responsibilities.
Ability to use multiple technology collaboration platforms, including collaboration tools. Examples: Microsoft Teams, Asana.
Ability to focus/concentrate on tasks and multi-task, when needed.
Begin work at the required time, per approved schedule.
Ability to lift/carry laptop and other mobile devices between work and home.
Ability to commute to work.
Ability to travel between National Academies’ facilities and offsite sponsor/partner locations.
Ability to work in different time zones, when travel is outside of current location, e.g., when traveling internationally.
Ability to perform work responsibilities onsite, where required.
Ability to interact in-person with multiple people and large groups.
Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and meet deadlines.

Work Environment

Hybrid office/telecommute environment; expected onsite percentage 60%. Occasional travel between National Academies’ facilities and to off-site meeting/sponsor locations.

Compensation & Benefits

An estimated compensation range for this position is $105,230 - $164,420. Compensation offered to the selected candidate will be based on the candidate’s relevant knowledge, skills, and work experience, commensurate with compensation of current employees in comparable positions with similar knowledge, skills, and work experience, and subject to budget parameters. Note it is not typical for a candidate to be hired at the higher end of the range. This is a benefits-eligible position. jobs.description:
Schneider Electric has a meaningful opportunity for a Project Manager, preferably in Nashville
, to join a high-visibility cost-transformation program. This role offers direct exposure to senior leadership and the opportunity to orchestrate a complex portfolio from idea through execution.

About The NAM ZBB Program

North America Operations is launching a zero-based review of how we organize and what we spend. Rather than adjusting last year’s budget up or down, zero-based budgeting methodology rebuilds the cost base from the work that actually needs to be done. The program covers two areas: organization (who does what work, and how much capacity we need) and spend (what we buy, and why). The first wave covers project execution and strategy roles across our Business Units, along with non-headcount spend in selected cost centers, and builds on a successful pilot in another Schneider Electric region.

The program is run by a small dedicated team – a Program lead, a Finance lead and an HR lead – working alongside an external consulting partner for the initial projects and to build the capabilities. The team reports to a Steering Committee that includes NAM Senior management.

Role Overview

You will be the program integrator and single point of accountability to the Steering Committee. You will own the program cadence, partner interfaces and system of management—moving every initiative from idea to commitment and execution.

Responsibilities

Own the overall program governance, operating cadence, and management system, including Steering Committees, workshops, and executive decision forums.
Develop, maintain, and communicate integrated program roadmaps, milestones, interdependencies, risks, and mitigation plans in close connection to Finance and HR
Lead enterprise-wide data collection efforts and activity assessments in partnership with external consulting teams.
Serve as the primary Schneider Electric program lead for the selected consulting firm, managing Statements of Work (SOWs), phase-gate reviews, deliverable acceptance, and financial milestones.
Partner with senior business leaders to secure executive sponsorship, accountability, and decision timelines for strategic initiatives; monitor progress from ideation through execution.
Drive initiative readiness for business and finance review, facilitating alignment with Business SVPs and Finance partners while proactively escalating decision bottlenecks and risks.
Coordinate cross-functional stakeholders across Finance, HR, Business Units, and external consulting partners to ensure successful program execution and value realization.
Track program performance, key decisions, action items, and execution outcomes, ensuring transparency, accountability, and timely delivery of objectives.

Skills and Competencies

Strong program leadership and integration skills across complex, cross-functional initiatives.
Executive presence and the ability to run effective senior-level decision forums.
Proven ability to influence without authority and establish accountability across a matrix organization.
Excellent planning, prioritization, dependency and risk-management capabilities.
Strong vendor-management skills, including scope, deliverables, acceptance criteria and commercial milestones.
Ability to translate complex program information into clear, executive-ready messages.
Comfortable leading through ambiguity, creating structure and working at pace.
Persistent, pragmatic, and results-oriented, with the judgment to escalate at the right time.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Operations, Engineering or a related field; MBA preferred.

Demonstrated experience leading enterprise-wide or cross-functional transformation programs.
Experience managing external consulting partners, statements of work and milestone-based deliverables.
Strong knowledge of program governance, decision management, risk management and executive reporting.
Experience in cost transformation, productivity programs or zero-based budgeting is a strong plus.
Experience in a matrixed multinational manufacturing or industrial organization preferred.
Advanced PowerPoint and Excel skills; experience with Power BI and program-management platforms is a plus.

What's in it for me?

Lead high-impact projects with visibility across the organization
Work with talented, collaborative teams in a culture that values innovation
Access to professional development opportunities and career growth pathways
Flexible work options that support work-life balance

Bring your project expertise to a team that's ready to welcome you — apply today!

At Schneider, we believe that every employee is a talent who deserves equal opportunities. This means you matter. Every individual needs to feel valued, supported, and treated fairly to do their best work.

Our Total Rewards is our way of saying: “We see you. We value you”. It’s more than just pay and benefits- it’s a meaningful investment in you. It is designed for you to perform, grow, feel safe, and elevate your potential to shine as an impact maker.

Schneider Electric is there when it matters most to you

Our Total Rewards package outlines all the benefits and support you’ll enjoy as part of the Schneider Electric team:

Care for Yourself and Your Family. We ensure you feel secure with benefits that help you and your family thrive: medical (with member reward points), dental, vision, and basic life insurance, Benefit Bucks, flexible work arrangements, paid family leaves, well-being programs, 12 holidays per year, and 15 days of paid time off per year.
