Active Top Secret/SCI Security Clearance and the ability to obtain and maintain a CI Poly
Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Information Systems, Computer Science, Information Assurance, Business, or a related discipline.
Twelve (12) years of progressively responsible experience in cybersecurity, information assurance, governance, risk, compliance, or related disciplines, including at least three (3) years of leadership experience managing technical teams or enterprise cybersecurity programs.
Above Experience to consist of:
NIST 800-53 and Risk Management Framework (RMF) based accreditations
Working in a classified environment consisting of multiple Collateral, SCI and/or SAP systems
Managing multiple projects at one time that could have many tasks within each.
Working with Windows operating systems
Developing standard operating procedures and system security plans
Supervising and mentoring ISSO level team

Self-motivated and possess good written, verbal, listening and presentation skills
Strong customer service, leadership and team building skills
Organizational skills to include attention to detail, time management, ability to multitask and prioritize.
Must live or relocate to a commutable distance of Beavercreek, Ohio

new_jobs.title: Staff Technical Program Manager, IT Audit & Governance
new_jobs.description:
We're looking for a senior, hands-on leader to own IT audit and governance across all of our applications, infrastructure, and systems. You'll be accountable for keeping IT audit-ready every day: SOX ITGCs and ITACs, plus the broader audit and governance obligations that touch the technology stack (SOC reports, ISO, security and regulatory audits).

This role is about accountability and execution. You'll work with cross-functional IT leaders across Infrastructure, Engineering, Security, Cloud, Enterprise Applications, and Business Systems to make sure controls are owned, operated, evidenced, and remediated on time. You'll also be the primary IT liaison to Internal Audit, Finance/SOX PMO, and external auditors. You operate independently, influence without authority, and can speak credibly with an engineer about a CI/CD pipeline and with the CAO about a deficiency.

We're looking to speak with candidates based in Palo Alto or New York City for our hybrid working model.

What You'll Do

Own audit and governance across all IT

Own the audit and governance program across all IT applications, infrastructure, cloud platforms, and supporting systems
Maintain a complete inventory of systems, owners, and applicable audit and compliance obligations (SOX, SOC 1/SOC 2, ISO 27001, and other regulatory or customer requirements)
Build and run an IT audit calendar that coordinates SOX, internal audit, external audit, and compliance activities to reduce duplicate asks and audit fatigue
Establish governance standards, policies, and control frameworks that apply consistently across IT

Drive accountability and execution with IT leaders

Partner with cross-functional IT leaders to assign clear control and remediation ownership, with defined deadlines and escalation paths
Run regular governance forums and control health reviews with IT leadership, reporting status, risks, and overdue items
Hold teams accountable for timely control execution, evidence quality, and issue closure, escalating early when commitments slip
Translate audit and compliance requirements into practical work that engineering and infrastructure teams can adopt without slowing delivery

Own ITGC and ITAC compliance

Own the end-to-end SOX IT program: scoping inputs, control design, ownership, evidence, readiness testing, and issue management
Maintain the ITGC framework (access management, change management, IT operations, SDLC) across all in-scope applications, databases, operating systems, and cloud infrastructure
Own ITAC strategy and coverage with Finance and business-system owners: automated controls, configurations, interfaces, calculations, and approval workflows
Own IPE/report validation, ITAC baselines, and segregation of duties (SoD) across ERP and key financial applications

Design, operate, and strengthen controls

Design controls that are engineered into IT workflows (ticketing, CI/CD, IAM, CMDB) rather than layered on manually
Run readiness and self-assessment testing ahead of Internal Audit and external auditor testing
Rationalize overlapping controls across frameworks so one control and one piece of evidence can satisfy multiple requirements
Drive automation and continuous control monitoring to reduce manual effort and audit burden
Manage SOC 1/SOC 2 report reviews, CUECs, and third-party/vendor control dependencies

Drive remediation and issue management

Own the issue lifecycle across IT, from identification and root cause through remediation plan, validation, and closure
Prepare management's response to audit findings and provide the IT perspective on deficiency severity with Finance, Legal, and Internal Audit
Report control health and remediation status to IT leadership, the CAO, and the Audit Committee as needed

Be the IT face to auditors and the business

Serve as primary IT contact for Internal Audit and external auditors on scope, walkthroughs, evidence requests, and reliance strategy
Coordinate PBC requests, evidence standards, and timelines across IT teams
Train and enable control owners and IT leaders on audit requirements, evidence quality, and their responsibilities

Lead and elevate the program

Set standards for control documentation, evidence, and issue management across IT
Mentor analysts and guide co-source or outsourced resources
Contribute to emerging governance areas such as AI/emerging technology

What You'll Bring

Required

8-12+ years of experience in IT audit, SOX compliance, IT governance, or technology risk (Big 4, internal audit, or in-house IT GRC)
Deep, hands-on experience with SOX 404 ITGCs and ITACs in a public company
Working knowledge of COSO, COBIT, and PCAOB AS 2201, and how external auditors approach IT reliance and ITAC testing
Experience across modern technology environments: cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP), SaaS, ERP (e.g., Oracle, NetSuite, SAP), infrastructure, and identity/access platforms
Familiarity with other frameworks and audits (SOC 1/SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST) and how to harmonize them
Proven track record of owning programs end-to-end and driving accountability and execution across multiple teams and senior leaders without direct authority
Excellent communication and executive presence, including negotiating with auditors and briefing senior leadership
Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Accounting, Computer Science, or a related field

Preferred

CISA, CISSP, CIA, CPA, or equivalent certification
Experience with GRC and audit tools (e.g., AuditBoard, ServiceNow GRC, Workiva, Archer)
Data analytics skills (SQL, Python, Power BI/Tableau) for full-population testing and control monitoring
Experience in high-growth, SaaS, or technology company environments
Familiarity with DevOps/CI-CD, infrastructure-as-code, and change management in agile environments

What Success Looks Like

First 90 days: Map the IT landscape, systems, control owners, and audit obligations. Build relationships with IT leaders, Finance, Internal Audit, and external auditors. Identify the top gaps, ownership issues, and quick wins.
6 months: Stand up a governance cadence with IT leaders, with clear ownership and on-time execution. Complete a full readiness cycle with controls evidenced on time and no surprises from auditors.
12 months: Reduce control count and manual effort through rationalization and automation, close prior-year findings, and establish a scalable, IT-owned audit and governance program with a consolidated audit calendar and framework

Full-time vacancy up to 12 months

The Information Systems and Technology (IS&T) Service supports the frontline policing and corporate operations of SAPOL through the provision of ICT infrastructure and communication platforms, operational software applications, and support services. The Service is responsible for driving the ongoing evolution of ICT capability across SAPOL, through the delivery of high-quality ICT change programs.

The Service is accountable for the successful delivery of business outcomes from a large portfolio of projects. It contains both project delivery accountability as well as portfolio governance responsibilities to manage quality, risk and budget to optimise outcomes from the portfolio as a whole. SAPOL is undertaking a large complex portfolio of work across a range of areas including core infrastructure, business systems and digital transformation initiatives.

Role Overview

As Project Manager, you will play a pivotal role in delivering technology solutions that support frontline policing operations, leading the end-to-end delivery of complex application and mobility-focused projects across SAPOL's fast-paced ICT portfolio. Working closely with project sponsors, business stakeholders, technical teams and external vendors, you will be responsible for delivering large-scale ICT initiatives that enhance operational capability, improve application performance and support critical policing services.

This role combines strong project leadership with stakeholder engagement, governance and delivery excellence. You will oversee all phases of the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC), including requirements gathering, solution design, development, testing, deployment and transition to operational support. Managing project plans, budgets, risks, resources and vendor outcomes, you will ensure solutions are delivered in line with business priorities, technical standards and organisational objectives. This senior position demands enterprise level and program experience.

Working within SAPOL's Mobility Portfolio, you will be responsible for managing projects that provide new capabilities for frontline police, accessed through mobile applications.

What You Need To Succeed

Considerable experience delivering large and complex ICT projects, ideally within government or similarly complex environments.
Proven ability to lead end-to-end project delivery, including project planning, scheduling, budget management, resource allocation, risk and issue management, scope control and stakeholder engagement.
Strong experience managing application-focused projects, with an understanding of application development methodologies, software delivery practices and the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC).
Experience delivering technology solutions that support business transformation, operational improvement and service delivery outcomes.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple stakeholders, including business leaders, technical teams, vendors and external partners, while maintaining positive working relationships and managing competing priorities.
Strong project governance and reporting capabilities, including the preparation and presentation of project updates, status reports and recommendations to executive and project governance forums.

new_jobs.title: Staff Technical Program Manager, IT Audit & Governance
new_jobs.description:
We're looking for a senior, hands-on leader to own IT audit and governance across all of our applications, infrastructure, and systems. You'll be accountable for keeping IT audit-ready every day: SOX ITGCs and ITACs, plus the broader audit and governance obligations that touch the technology stack (SOC reports, ISO, security and regulatory audits).

This role is about accountability and execution. You'll work with cross-functional IT leaders across Infrastructure, Engineering, Security, Cloud, Enterprise Applications, and Business Systems to make sure controls are owned, operated, evidenced, and remediated on time. You'll also be the primary IT liaison to Internal Audit, Finance/SOX PMO, and external auditors. You operate independently, influence without authority, and can speak credibly with an engineer about a CI/CD pipeline and with the CAO about a deficiency.

We're looking to speak with candidates based in Palo Alto or New York City for our hybrid working model.

What You'll Do

Own audit and governance across all IT

Own the audit and governance program across all IT applications, infrastructure, cloud platforms, and supporting systems
Maintain a complete inventory of systems, owners, and applicable audit and compliance obligations (SOX, SOC 1/SOC 2, ISO 27001, and other regulatory or customer requirements)
Build and run an IT audit calendar that coordinates SOX, internal audit, external audit, and compliance activities to reduce duplicate asks and audit fatigue
Establish governance standards, policies, and control frameworks that apply consistently across IT

Drive accountability and execution with IT leaders

Partner with cross-functional IT leaders to assign clear control and remediation ownership, with defined deadlines and escalation paths
Run regular governance forums and control health reviews with IT leadership, reporting status, risks, and overdue items
Hold teams accountable for timely control execution, evidence quality, and issue closure, escalating early when commitments slip
Translate audit and compliance requirements into practical work that engineering and infrastructure teams can adopt without slowing delivery

Own ITGC and ITAC compliance

Own the end-to-end SOX IT program: scoping inputs, control design, ownership, evidence, readiness testing, and issue management
Maintain the ITGC framework (access management, change management, IT operations, SDLC) across all in-scope applications, databases, operating systems, and cloud infrastructure
Own ITAC strategy and coverage with Finance and business-system owners: automated controls, configurations, interfaces, calculations, and approval workflows
Own IPE/report validation, ITAC baselines, and segregation of duties (SoD) across ERP and key financial applications

Design, operate, and strengthen controls

Design controls that are engineered into IT workflows (ticketing, CI/CD, IAM, CMDB) rather than layered on manually
Run readiness and self-assessment testing ahead of Internal Audit and external auditor testing
Rationalize overlapping controls across frameworks so one control and one piece of evidence can satisfy multiple requirements
Drive automation and continuous control monitoring to reduce manual effort and audit burden
Manage SOC 1/SOC 2 report reviews, CUECs, and third-party/vendor control dependencies

Drive remediation and issue management

Own the issue lifecycle across IT, from identification and root cause through remediation plan, validation, and closure
Prepare management's response to audit findings and provide the IT perspective on deficiency severity with Finance, Legal, and Internal Audit
Report control health and remediation status to IT leadership, the CAO, and the Audit Committee as needed

Be the IT face to auditors and the business

Serve as primary IT contact for Internal Audit and external auditors on scope, walkthroughs, evidence requests, and reliance strategy
Coordinate PBC requests, evidence standards, and timelines across IT teams
Train and enable control owners and IT leaders on audit requirements, evidence quality, and their responsibilities

Lead and elevate the program

Set standards for control documentation, evidence, and issue management across IT
Mentor analysts and guide co-source or outsourced resources
Contribute to emerging governance areas such as AI/emerging technology

What You'll Bring

Required

8-12+ years of experience in IT audit, SOX compliance, IT governance, or technology risk (Big 4, internal audit, or in-house IT GRC)
Deep, hands-on experience with SOX 404 ITGCs and ITACs in a public company
Working knowledge of COSO, COBIT, and PCAOB AS 2201, and how external auditors approach IT reliance and ITAC testing
Experience across modern technology environments: cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP), SaaS, ERP (e.g., Oracle, NetSuite, SAP), infrastructure, and identity/access platforms
Familiarity with other frameworks and audits (SOC 1/SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST) and how to harmonize them
Proven track record of owning programs end-to-end and driving accountability and execution across multiple teams and senior leaders without direct authority
Excellent communication and executive presence, including negotiating with auditors and briefing senior leadership
Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Accounting, Computer Science, or a related field

Preferred

CISA, CISSP, CIA, CPA, or equivalent certification
Experience with GRC and audit tools (e.g., AuditBoard, ServiceNow GRC, Workiva, Archer)
Data analytics skills (SQL, Python, Power BI/Tableau) for full-population testing and control monitoring
Experience in high-growth, SaaS, or technology company environments
Familiarity with DevOps/CI-CD, infrastructure-as-code, and change management in agile environments

What Success Looks Like

First 90 days: Map the IT landscape, systems, control owners, and audit obligations. Build relationships with IT leaders, Finance, Internal Audit, and external auditors. Identify the top gaps, ownership issues, and quick wins.
6 months: Stand up a governance cadence with IT leaders, with clear ownership and on-time execution. Complete a full readiness cycle with controls evidenced on time and no surprises from auditors.
12 months: Reduce control count and manual effort through rationalization and automation, close prior-year findings, and establish a scalable, IT-owned audit and governance program with a consolidated audit calendar and framework

About MIB

At MIB our people are passionate about making roads safer by getting uninsured and hit-and-run drivers off our roads. Working in partnership with the Police, Insurers and Government our collective aim is to make it a thing of the past but, until that’s accomplished, we’re here to compensate victims quickly, fairly and compassionately.

Last year we helped more than 34,000 people struck by uninsured and hit-and-run drivers and paid over £400 million in compensation to support victims rebuild their lives.

About The Role

Are you passionate about information security and helping organisations build secure, resilient ways of working?

As Information Security Manager
, you'll play a pivotal role in supporting MIB's client companies to strengthen their security posture, manage risk with confidence and embed effective security practices across their organisations.

Acting as a trusted advisor and subject matter expert, you'll provide specialist guidance, assurance and project support, helping client companies develop and maintain proportionate security policies, standards, controls and frameworks that align with their business objectives and contractual obligations.

This is an influential role where you'll work closely with stakeholders to ensure information security risks are understood, managed effectively and integrated into everyday operations. You'll help organisations protect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of their information and systems, enabling them to operate securely in an increasingly complex threat landscape.

If you enjoy building trusted relationships, translating security requirements into practical business solutions and making a tangible impact across multiple organisations, this is an exciting opportunity to shape and strengthen information security at a strategic level.

This Will Be Achieved By

Providing a focal point within MIB for client company information security guidance, assurance and subject matter expertise.
Supporting the alignment of client company information security activity to agreed client company objectives and obligations.
Supporting an effective information security risk management approach for client companies, helping assess information security risks, agree proportionate treatment plans and track progress to closure.

Key Responsibilities

General

Support the Head of Information Security and the Information Security GRC Manager by providing client company insight to inform the wider security strategy where relevant.
Share knowledge, guidance and good practice with colleagues supporting client company information security activity.
Work with Security Operations, Engineering and Architecture functions to ensure client company requirements are understood and appropriately reflected in advice, assurance and control recommendations.
Provide client company teams with security-focused support, training and consultancy to help them understand and meet applicable security standards, policies and legislation.
Engage with ODT leadership, supporting functions and business stakeholders to support the delivery of effective information security practices within client companies.
Produce and share management information on the performance of client company information security controls, providing assurance on maturity, risk exposure and control effectiveness.
Recommend improvements to client company information security standards, guidance and control expectations through continuous improvement activity.
Develop and maintain procedures and guidance that help client companies understand and respond to relevant threats and vulnerabilities.
Support client companies to embed appropriate information security behaviours and practices that help protect their information and information systems.
Review and advise on information security clauses, obligations and controls within client company contracts.
Keep up to date with emerging trends, technologies and legislation relevant to client company information security and assurance.
Act as the client company point of contact for information security governance, risk, assurance and compliance matters.
Support client company governance forums by providing clear reporting, insight and challenge on key information security risks, audit outcomes, control maturity and remediation progress.
Support the development, review and alignment of client company information security policies, standards, procedures and guidance.
Maintain a proportionate client company information security risk and compliance approach, including information security risk assessments, treatment plans, escalation, tracking and a rolling compliance schedule.
Review, challenge and track client company control actions, vulnerabilities and information security incidents to ensure appropriate mitigation and management focus.
Coordinate client company audit and assurance activity, including audit readiness, evidence quality, audit findings, remediation plans and action closure.
Measure and report on the performance and compliance of key client company information security controls, including policy, process and relevant technical control expectations.
Support client company initiatives, solutions and services where information security advice, assurance or oversight is required.

A thorough understanding of the information security threat landscape, significant risks, technical developments and regulatory expectations as they apply to client company environments.
Strong interpersonal and stakeholder management skills are essential, as the role must influence and support client company teams and stakeholders without direct ownership of their operational delivery.
Extensive experience as an information security practitioner, ideally within a complex supplier, client or multi-stakeholder environment.
Direct experience of supporting information security governance, risk and compliance activity in a stakeholder-facing or advisory capacity.
Experience and knowledge of supporting information security risk assessments, including review, challenge and assurance of risk treatment plans.
Proven experience of developing or supporting information security policies, procedures, standards and guidance.
Experience supporting ISO27001-aligned controls, assurance activity or equivalent information security frameworks.
Ability to harness the commitment and contribution of colleagues outside the direct span of control.
Excellent written and oral communication skills.
Ability to research, assess and recommend improvements to governance, risk and compliance capabilities and maturity.
Ability to present ideas in non-technical, business-friendly and accessible language.
Ability to effectively prioritise and execute tasks in a high-pressure environment.

new_jobs.title: Sr Program Manager, MX Holiday & Contingency
new_jobs.description:
Description

Want to work at a company that aims to be Earth's most customer-centric? Then meet Amazon. Amazon has spent more than 25 years inventing on behalf of customers and is now one of the world's largest online retailers and marketplaces. Our entrepreneurial culture has produced new products and services such as Echo and Amazon Web Services.

The Holiday and Contingency Planning (HCP) team coordinates Amazon's operational response to holidays, planned events and unplanned contingencies. The goal is to protect the customer experience and limit operational impact, balancing reliability against speed. As a central coordination team, HCP plans and executes network configuration changes that adjust customer promises and package flow, so the network keeps performing and recovers quickly from disruption.

We are hiring an HCP Program Manager in Mexico to own contingency management for the Mexico network and support HCP programs across LATAM. Mexico's network faces many kinds of disruption: national and state holidays, peak events such as Hot Sale and El Buen Fin, Semana Santa and Día de Muertos, hurricanes and floods, road blockades and civil demonstrations, and cross-border (US–MX) flow disruptions. You will work with stakeholders across all miles and lines of business, including Middle Mile/ATS and Relay Operations, Last Mile (AMZL and DSP network), Fulfillment and Sort Centers, First Mile/3P, Regional Planning and Business Continuity teams. You will also partner with Legal, Public Policy, PXT and Tech teams, and with the global HCP team in India and other regions.

We're looking for a hands-on, motivated self-starter who is passionate about using data to make quick decisions and who exemplifies "Bias for Action" and "Are Right, A Lot." The successful candidate has strong analytical and problem-solving skills, is detail-oriented, and is comfortable working with large data sets. They communicate complex analysis clearly, build strong relationships with stakeholders, and drive toward simple, scalable solutions to difficult problems.

Key job responsibilities

Based in Mexico, or open to relocation
Own the end-to-end holiday planning & contingency management for Mexico: plan the holiday and event calendar, assess risk, define the network response (promise, capacity and flow changes), execute it, and run post-event reviews.
Lead real-time response to unplanned disruptions such as weather, blockades and carrier or site outages. Coordinate decisions across miles and drive fast recovery.
Analyze historical event performance, including delivery experience, promise accuracy, backlog and recovery time. Turn the analysis into recommendations for senior leadership.
Build and improve the team's reporting tools, mechanisms and processes so internal and external partners get more actionable, granular data.
Drive the operating cadence: WBR/MBR inputs, goal setting, goal tracking and process improvement for HCP Mexico.
Standardize and scale HCP mechanisms across LATAM. Bring best practices from other regions and share Mexico learnings with the global team.
Communicate complex analyses and decisions clearly, in writing and verbally, in Spanish and English, to audiences from operations teams to senior leaders.

A day in the life

You start by checking the risk outlook for the coming days: upcoming holidays, weather alerts and planned demonstrations. You align with Middle Mile, Last Mile and site operations on any network changes needed, then go deeper on data to size a promise adjustment for an upcoming peak or holiday. You might lead a cross-functional event review, write the narrative for leadership, or work with tech partners to automate a manual step in the contingency process. When something unexpected happens, you coordinate the response and keep stakeholders informed until the network recovers.

About The Team

HCP is a ROW team spanning operations, program management and tech, with members in India and LATAM. We value bias for action, being right a lot, and simple, scalable solutions to complex problems.

**Inclusive team culture**

At Amazon we embrace our differences and are committed to furthering our culture of inclusion, reinforced by our Leadership Principles, which remind team members to seek diverse perspectives, learn and be curious, and earn trust.

**Mentorship & career growth**

The team has a broad mix of experience levels and tenures. We celebrate knowledge sharing and mentorship, and assign projects with each team member's growth in mind.

Basic Qualifications

5+ years of program or project management experience
Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
Experience owning program strategy, end-to-end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
Bachelor's degree or equivalent
Speak, write, and read fluently in English, and have the ability to take direction in English

Preferred Qualifications

3+ years of driving process improvements experience
Master's degree, or MBA in business, operations, human resources, adult education, organizational development, instructional design or related field
3+ years of stakeholder management experience

new_jobs.title: Regulatory Implementation Manager
new_jobs.description:
Medica is a nonprofit health plan with more than a million members that serves communities in Minnesota, Nebraska, Wisconsin, Missouri, and beyond. We deliver personalized health care experiences and partner closely with providers to ensure members are genuinely cared for.

We're a team that owns our work with accountability, makes data-driven decisions, embraces continuous learning, and celebrates collaboration — because success is a team sport. It's our mission to be there in the moments that matter most for our members and employees. Join us in creating a community of connected care, where coordinated, quality service is the norm and every member feels valued.

The Regulatory Implementation Manager provides enterprise leadership for complex, cross-functional regulatory implementation initiatives. This role translates emerging regulatory requirements, legislation, and compliance guidance into actionable enterprise strategies, implementation plans, governance structures, and operational requirements.

The Regulatory Implementation Manager works in close partnership with the Director and coordinates execution across Compliance, Legal, Public Affairs, Information Technology, Marketing, Product, and other business functions. The role assesses regulatory and business impacts, identifies risks and dependencies, establishes implementation priorities, and advises senior leaders on regulatory implementation strategy, organizational readiness, resource requirements, risks, and decisions requiring executive action.

In this role, you will establish consistent regulatory implementation standards, governance practices, decision rights, operating guardrails, and reporting mechanisms supporting timely, sustainable, and well-controlled execution. The role also provides enterprise oversight of Medicare Marketing Materials and serves as a subject-matter resource for regulatory change management, implementation strategy, and organizational readiness. Performs other duties as assigned.

Key Accountabilities

Management & Leadership
Leads the Regulatory Implementation team and establishes clear accountabilities, priorities, performance expectations, and operating rhythms
Coaches and develops staff, defines team roles and responsibilities, and allocates resources to meet enterprise regulatory priorities
Builds a culture of accountability, collaboration, sound judgment, and service excellence

Regulatory Strategy & Impact Assessment
Provides strategic regulatory implementation guidance across Medica
Proactively assesses and communicates new regulatory requirements, legislation, and compliance bulletins on enterprise implications
Interprets requirements, identifies business impacts, priorities, risks, and resource needs, and develops recommendations for enterprise implementation

Implementation Strategy & Design
Leads the development of enterprise implementation strategies, operating models, readiness activities, and delivery approaches for complex regulatory initiatives
Coordinates business and technology dependencies and ensures regulatory requirements are translated into executable and sustainable operational changes
Monitors implementation progress, risks, resource requirements, and organizational readiness through completion

Medicare Marketing Materials Oversight
Responsible for oversight of Medicare Marketing Materials regulatory requirements and implementation
Establishes governance, review processes, controls, and accountability to support compliant and timely development, review, approval, and submission activities
Partners with Legal, Compliance, Marketing, Product, and other stakeholders to identify risks, resolve issues, and ensure regulatory readiness

Regulatory Expertise & Knowledge Sharing
Builds and advances organizational capability in regulatory implementation through standards, training, lessons learned, and knowledge sharing
Coach teams and implementation professionals on regulatory interpretation, governance, and execution
Promotes consistent application of enterprise practices and incorporates insights from regulatory developments into team and organizational priorities

Enterprise Governance & Operating Model
Establishes enterprise governance, decision rights, implementation standards, and operational guardrails for regulatory initiatives, including reporting
Defines roles and responsibilities across Compliance and business partners to support consistent and accountable execution
Develops and maintains the enterprise Regulatory Implementation roadmap and governance framework

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in related field
7+ years of work experience beyond degree
Demonstrated experience leading and developing teams and influencing cross-functional partners
Strong knowledge of healthcare regulations and compliance requirements and the ability to interpret and apply regulatory guidance
Experience developing implementation strategies, governance practices, roadmaps, budgets, resource plans, and risk mitigation strategies
Previous experience overseeing regulatory requirements affecting Medicare Marketing Materials

Preferred Qualifications

Strong leadership, communication, problem-solving, analytical, and decision-making skills
Demonstrated ability to partner effectively with Information Technology and business leaders on complex enterprise initiatives
Highest standard of ethics, accountability, discipline, and professionalism

This position is an Office role, which requires an employee to work onsite, on average, 3 days per week. We are open to candidates located near one of the following office locations: Minnetonka, MN, Madison, WI, St. Louis, MO, or Omaha, NE.

The full salary grade for this position is $88,800 - $152,300. While the full salary grade is provided, the typical hiring salary range for this role is expected to be between $88,800 - $133,245. Annual salary range placement will depend on a variety of factors including, but not limited to, education, work experience, applicable certifications and/or licensure, the position's scope and responsibility, internal pay equity and external market salary data.  In addition to base compensation, this position may be eligible for incentive plan compensation in addition to base salary. Medica offers a generous total rewards package that includes competitive medical, dental, vision, PTO, Holidays, paid volunteer time off, 401K contributions, caregiver services and many other benefits to support our employees.

The compensation and benefits information is provided as of the date of this posting. Medica’s compensation and benefits are subject to change at any time, with or without notice, subject to applicable law.

Eligibility to work in the US:
Medica does not offer work visa sponsorship for this role. All candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of application. Employment is contingent on verification of identity and eligibility to work in the United States.

A Little Bit About Us

Nestlé Nespresso SA is a pioneer and is widely regarded as one of the top references in the field of high-quality portioned coffee. The company works with more than 130 000 farmers in 18 countries through the Nespresso Sustainable Quality Plan to embed sustainability practices on farms and the surrounding landscapes. Launched in 2003 in collaboration with the NGO Rainforest Alliance, the Nespresso Plan helps to improve the yield and quality of harvests, ensuring a sustainable supply of high-quality coffee and improving livelihoods of farmers and their communities.

In 2022, Nespresso achieved B Corp™ certification – joining an international movement of over 10’000 purpose-led businesses that meet B Corp’s high standards of social and environmental responsibility and transparency.

Headquartered in Vevey, Switzerland, Nespresso operates in 98 markets and has over 14'000 employees. In 2025, it operated a global retail network of 849 boutiques. For more information, visit the Nespresso website: www.nespresso.com.

Position Summary:

We’re looking for a curious, strategic Consumer & Market Insights Manager
to join our Insights & Analytics team at Nespresso Canada and turn consumer understanding into opportunities that shape our future.

As Consumer & Market Insights Manager
, you will report to the Insights & Analytics Manager, and you’ll shape and lead the integrated insights agenda for Nespresso Canada, transforming complex consumer, market, customer, and competitive data into clear strategic recommendations. The City of London Corporation is currently undergoing a programme to ensure that our pay and reward practices are competitive and equitable across the whole organisation to ensure that everyone has the opportunity to thrive in the work that we do.

Who are we?

As City of London Police, we protect the people, businesses and infrastructure of the City of London, one of the most important and dynamic environments in the UK and globally. London City is the smallest borough in London, so does that make our job any less challenging? Absolutely not – because there’s so much going on.

City of London Police play a vital role in keeping the City of London diverse community safe. As a Police Staff Member you will be helping to making the city safer and deliver a valued service for those that live, work and visit the City.

Hybrid working -
This Police Staff role adheres to Corporation of London’s hybrid working policy, which requires a 60% office attendance rate. The specifics of this will be discussed locally with your hiring manager if you’re successful for the role.

The City of London Police is keen to promote flexible working and will, subject to operational policing requirements, proactively consider all applications to work flexibly.

The City of London Police is committed to equality of opportunities and continuously strive for inclusivity within our Force.

About The Team

The Domestic Corruption Unit (DCU), serves as the national coordinating function for domestic bribery and corruption in support of His Majesty's Government's Anti-Corruption Strategy. The unit receives and assesses referrals from police forces, public sector organisations, partner agencies, and private industry, undertaking triage and development work to determine investigative viability, threat, risk, and harm. Where appropriate, the DCU either conducts investigations directly or supports the allocation of matters to local forces, regional organised crime units, or other partner agencies, while providing ongoing specialist advice and oversight.

In addition to its investigative role, the DCU works closely with national partners, including the Joint Anti-Corruption Unit (JACU) and the National Economic Crime Centre (NECC), to improve understanding of the domestic corruption threat and identify systemic vulnerabilities. The unit also has a strong focus on prevention and disruption, using intelligence and insight to identify emerging risks, strengthen institutional integrity, and support improvements in policy, practice, and capability across policing and partner organisations, thereby enhancing the UK's overall response to domestic bribery and corruption.

NLF ONLY:
You can find out more about working within National Lead Force here- https://vimeo.com/1124775531/c2ea98aee0?share=copy

About The Role

The Intelligence Analyst will be responsible for providing dedicated analytical support to the Domestic Corruption Unit (DCU) in understanding the domestic corruption threat and in the investigation of bribery, corruption, money laundering, and associated criminality.

The candidate will be responsible for the production of crime and intelligence products in line with the National Intelligence Model (NIM). The candidate will be expected to identify and develop enforcement, disruption and prevention opportunities through analysis. Findings will be utilised by the DCU, wider law enforcement and the counter corruption community to disrupt and prevent criminals from committing bribery and corruption. The role would benefit from a candidate with good analytical experience in supporting investigations who is able to operate effectively from the outset.

Responsibilities

In this role, you will be:

Collate, evaluate and analyse information from a variety of internal and external sources, producing high quality analytical products, contributing to the development of strategies and identification of enforcement, disruption and prevention opportunities.
Applying analytical techniques, to develop crime and intelligence packages, compliant with the NIM for dissemination to law enforcement and the wider counter corruption community.
As appropriate, to maximise intelligence sharing opportunities to develop the unit’s capability, as well as informing stakeholder initiatives/strategies.
Conduct evidential analysis and attend court to give evidence.
Undertake any other duties commensurate with the role and grade as reasonably requested by line management.

Requirements

Your application will be scored against the criteria listed below for shortlisting. Please give examples and evidence your ability, knowledge and experience against the points below in your application.

Excellent research and analytical skills to identify the required information to facilitate accurate assessments of bribery and corruption.
Excellent report writing skills to provide key information in relation to the assessment decision that is both clear and auditable.
Good decision-making skills and the ability to communicate decisions to stakeholder groups and effectively manage their expectations.
A proven analytical background, together with knowledge of criminal investigations, practices and processes.

This vacancy is open only to those who have the right to work in the UK.
Due to security vetting requirements for this being MV/SC, applicants must have continuously resided in the UK for the 5 years immediately preceding their application. Unfortunately, we are unable to progress applications that do not meet this requirement.

th November 2026 @ 23:59

About The Role

Sportradar supplies betting operators around the world with odds and trading services. Our clients share a portion of the revenue generated from bets placed through our services and, as part of their contract with Sportradar, are required to report all relevant betting activity to us. Revenue Protection Team makes sure this activity is reported accurately and in line with those contractual obligations.

You will work with large sets of client betting data to identify gaps, discrepancies or unusual patterns and investigate their cause. You will determine what the contract requires, gather the supporting evidence and estimate the potential commercial impact. You will build a clear case for Sales and Legal to take forward with the client, then follow each case through to resolution and measure the outcome.

This is not a trading role.
You will not be pricing markets or managing betting liabilities. The focus is on data investigation, building evidence and revenue recovery
.

THE CHALLENGE

Analyse client betting data to spot anomalies and changes in behaviour.
Compare clients against their peers and against their own history to tell a real problem from a seasonal or market effect.
Build the evidence behind each finding so that it stands up to challenge.
Estimate the revenue impact of an infringement using a clear and defensible method.
Write short, precise findings for non-technical stakeholders in Sales, Legal and management.
Build and improve the tools the team uses for recurring checks, including AI assisted ones.
Follow a case through to resolution and measure the uplift afterwards.

About You

2+ years of experience in a data-led investigative role. Experience in betting or sports data is preferred, but we also welcome strong backgrounds in fraud, risk, financial crime, payments, revenue assurance, trading risk, integrity or similar areas.
Proven ability to uncover wrongdoing, non-compliance or revenue leakage through data analysis, from the first signal to an evidenced and quantified conclusion.
Strong Excel skills, including pivot tables, lookups, cleaning and reconciling large datasets, and building calculations that others can review and validate. Your Excel skills will be assessed as part of the interview process.
Working knowledge of SQL, with the ability to pull, filter and aggregate data from large tables independently.
Clear and concise writing skills, with the ability to explain complex findings to people who may not know the underlying data.
Curiosity and persistence, with the drive to keep digging until the explanation holds.
An interest in using and building tools, including AI, to work more effectively, applying them alongside your own knowledge, skills and informed judgement rather than as a substitute for them.

Nice to have

Python for data analysis.
Power BI or a similar tool.
Experience writing to or dealing with external clients on contractual matters.

Our Offer

A collaborative environment with colleagues from all over the world (Offices in Europe, Asia and US) including various social events and teambuilding.
Flexibility to manage your workday and tasks with autonomy.
A balance of structure and autonomy to tackle your daily tasks.

Calm and Reulay app (leading well-being apps designed to support focus, quality rest, mindfulness, and long-term mental resilience).

For this reason, we are an office-first business operating on a fully on-site model, with team members working in the office five days a week to build relationships, exchange ideas, and grow together.

As a security first organization, UC Digital Risk & Security (UCDRS) is part of the Digital Innovation & Technology (DigIT) Department. The UCDRS teams include UCOP local and system-wide information security and risk teams focused on providing cyber security services to the UC system. We maintain an innovative, inclusive, and supportive work environment.

Position Summary

Reporting to the Deputy Chief Information Security Officer, the Security Operations Manager is responsible for monitoring, detecting, protecting, and maintaining the security of data, systems, and networks at UCOP. This role includes managing the UCOP Security Operations team, monitoring the UCOP infrastructure for malicious activity, developing and implementing security processes and procedures, managing vulnerabilities, and coordinating security incident response. The Security Operations Manager will work closely with other units at UCOP, including infrastructure and application development teams, desktop engineering, and the service desk, to identify vulnerabilities, implement best practices, and ensure the security of the UCOP computing environment.

Key Responsibilities

50% Responsible for managing the daily activities of Security Operations security analysts who plan, design, develop, implement and maintain systems and programs to ensure the integrity, reliability and security of UCOP data and systems, and monitor and respond to threats to the UCOP computing environment. Responsible for providing research, analysis and solutions to address attempted efforts to compromise security protocols. Proactively addresses the negative impact on Office of the President caused by theft, destruction, alteration or denial of access of information. Advises departments on security prevention, best practices and secure software.

10% Designs, configures and manages complex security systems including data loss prevention software, security information and event management systems, vulnerability scanners, and endpoint security agents. Administers security configurations to control access to information systems and networks including on premise and cloud environments.

10% Directs incident response and forensic investigations and addresses and produces reports in response to highly complex or broad-scale security incidents. Company Overview

IDMe is the next-generation digital identity wallet that simplifies how individuals securely prove their identity online. Consumers can verify their identity with IDMe once and seamlessly login across websites without having to create a new login and verify their identity again. Over 175 million users experience streamlined login and identity verification with IDMe at 22 federal agencies, 50 state government agencies, and more than 100 healthcare organizations. Over 600 consumer brands use IDMe to verify communities and user segments to honor service and build more authentic relationships. IDMe’s technology meets the federal standards for consumer authentication set by the Commerce Department and is approved as a NIST 800-63-3 IAL2 / AAL2 credential service provider by the Kantara Initiative. IDMe is committed to “No Identity Left Behind” to enable all people to have a secure digital identity. To learn more, visit https://network.id.me/.

IDMe is a full-time, in-office culture. Unless a specific job description explicitly states otherwise, all roles are on-site five days per week at one of our offices in McLean, VA; Mountain View, CA; New York City, NY; or Tampa, FL. Certain roles — such as field-based sales or other remote-by-design positions — may have different work arrangements as noted in their individual postings.

At IDMe, we embrace the thoughtful use of AI tools in our daily work and there are even occasions where we leverage AI in our hiring process. However, during the interview process, we want to understand your individual skills and experiences. Therefore, we have guidelines on how AI can be appropriately used during your application and interviews which can be found here.

Role Overview

ID.me is looking for a Senior Fraud Investigations Analyst
to join our organization as an execution-focused individual contributor. This role is responsible for leading investigations into account takeover (ATO) activity, identifying fraud patterns at scale, and strengthening detection strategies.

We are seeking a highly skilled analyst who can independently analyze large datasets, uncover coordinated fraud campaigns, and drive improvements in detection systems. This role requires moving beyond case-by-case investigation into trend analysis, signal development, and data-driven decision making.

This role is based out of our McLean, VA office and requires full-time in-office attendance.

Responsibilities

Lead complex account takeover (ATO) investigations, including multi-account and organized fraud activity
Analyze large datasets using SQL, Python, or similar tools to identify trends, anomalies, and attack patterns
Use fraud detection tools, machine learning outputs, and risk-scoring systems to drive high-quality investigations
Independently own investigations from detection through resolution, including clear documentation and recommendations
Identify gaps in detection logic and contribute to improvements in rules, models, and workflows
Partner with engineering, data, and product teams to enhance fraud detection capabilities and signal quality
Act as an escalation point for high-severity or ambiguous fraud cases
Develop and refine investigation playbooks and analytical approaches for ATO detection
Support reporting and analysis of fraud trends, detection performance, and operational metrics
Leverage AI/LLM tools to analyze large datasets, identify fraud patterns, and improve investigation speed and accuracy while validating outputs against source data

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution; strong preference for quantitative fields such as Economics, Computer Science, Statistics, Mathematics, or similar
4+ years of experience in fraud investigations, threat intelligence, cybersecurity, or risk management, with a focus on account takeover (ATO) attacks (typically 4–8 years total experience; candidates should have <10 years overall) 2+ years of experience using SQL, Python, or similar tools to analyze data and drive investigations
2+ years of hands-on experience using fraud detection tools, machine learning models, or risk-scoring methodologies
2+ years of experience interpreting fraud indicators, behavioral signals, or transaction monitoring data
Demonstrated experience analyzing fraud trends beyond individual case investigations (e.g., pattern detection, ring analysis)
Experience using AI/LLM tools to enhance data analysis and investigations, with demonstrated ability to validate and apply outputs effectively

Preferred Qualifications

Experience at a fintech company, technology company, or reputable financial institution
Strong experience analyzing organized fraud rings or large-scale ATO campaigns
Experience influencing fraud detection logic, models, or rule systems
Familiarity with AI/ML techniques applied to fraud detection and risk analysis
Ability to translate analytical findings into actionable improvements for product, engineering, or risk systems

The annual base salary listed does not include a company bonus, incentive for sales roles, equity and benefits which will be determined based on experience, skills, education, relevant training, geographic location and role.

IDMe offers comprehensive medical, dental, vision, health savings account, flexible spending accounts (medical, limited purpose, dependent care, commuter benefit accounts), basic and voluntary life and AD&D insurance, 401(k) with company match, parental leave, ability to participate in unlimited paid time off subject to the terms and conditions of the PTO policy, including 8 company wide holidays, short and long-term disability insurance, accident and critical illness insurance, referral bonus policy, employee assistance program, pet insurance, travel assistant program, wellbeing and childcare discounts, benefit advocates, and a learning and development benefit.

$90,000—$120,000 USD

new_jobs.description:
For questions regarding this position, please contact the Recruiter listed in the Supplemental Information section.

About The Position

Riverside University Health System (RUHS) seeks candidates for an RUHS Compliance Program Manager position. This role supports the development, coordination, implementation, and oversight of RUHS corporate compliance programs and activities. The selected candidate will supervise support staff, ensure adherence to applicable regulations, and perform related duties as required. Current certification in Healthcare Privacy Compliance (CHPC)
is strongly preferred.

Key Responsibilities Include

Supporting compliance with federal, state, and county laws and regulations, including HITECH.
Providing subject matter expertise on medical privacy and information security.
Overseeing staff and managing program activities as assigned.
Assisting in achieving compliance goals and strategic objectives.

The RUHS Compliance Program Manager is a journey-level manager classification reporting to the RUHS/County Compliance and Privacy Officer. Incumbents are expected to perform complex and increasingly responsible work with minimal supervision, contributing to the design, execution, and monitoring of effective compliance programs. This position is distinct from the RUHS/County Compliance and Privacy Officer, which entails broader responsibilities in directing and managing regulatory compliance programs.

This class has been deemed eligible for the Performance Recognition Plan as set forth under Article 3, Section 311(C) of the County Management Resolution. Program eligibility requires employees to be in a leadership position, manage other employees or programs, and have significant influence on the achievement of organizational objectives.

Why RUHS Medical Center?

Riverside University Health System-Medical Center is nationally recognized for its innovative, progressive care and is considered one of the top employers in the region. The 439-bed Medical Center is a designated Stroke Center, Level I Trauma Center, and home to the only Pediatric ICU in the area.

For more information about RUHS Medical Center, please visit ruhealth.org .

Examples Of Essential Duties

Perform audits to assess compliance with various laws, regulations, policies, and standards such as those related to healthcare fraud, waste and abuse, billing and coding, clinical documentation, privacy and information security, research and ethics; maintain a system of reporting that provides timely and relevant information of all aspects of compliance issues.
Participate in appropriate level of response, develop corrective action plans and conduct compliance investigations while maintaining confidentiality of information reported, as appropriate.
Evaluate departmental continuous readiness to achieve compliance in the areas of healthcare privacy and security; assist in the development and implementation of privacy policies, procedures and breach notification as necessary.
Develop and implement policies and procedures for filing and investigation of complaints related to HIPAA/HITECH Privacy, Breach Notification Rules and related County guidelines and procedures.
Develop and monitor policies and procedures that establish standards for ensuring patient privacy protections, including by providing guidance to individual employees and departments on the HIPAA Privacy Rule, as appropriate.
Document and retain all complaints received as required by HIPAA/HITECH; establish and maintain a mechanism for tracking and reporting the investigation and resolving such complaints.
Develop and administer training for RUHS staff to promote awareness of compliance to regulatory standards.
Provide guidance and assistance to departments on a variety of privacy and compliance auditing, and internal control matters; document findings and prepare reports.
Supervise, assign, review, and evaluate the work performed by staff; direct the day-to-day operations of support staff.

Minimum Qualifications

Education:
Graduation from an accredited college or university with a bachelor's degree, preferably with a major in business administration, public administration, public health nursing, finance, accounting, or a closely related field to the assignment. (A master's degree from an accredited college or university in any of the aforementioned majors is preferred.) Possession of current Healthcare Privacy Compliance (CHPC) certification is preferred.

Experience:
Three years of professional, journey-level experience in healthcare compliance, which includes internal auditing experience and experience in the development and implementation of HIPAA and/or privacy compliance programs.

Knowledge of:
Information security; theory, principles and practices of general healthcare; governmental accounting, budgeting and auditing; HIPAA privacy and security rules and regulations; privacy laws, rules and regulations relating to information and security; federal, state and local codes, rules and regulations including healthcare fiscal operations; the methods of developing systems forms for various types of accounting records and reports; information systems and their application to accounting operations; the principles, methods and techniques of public administration, personnel and business office management; the principles and techniques of supervision.

Ability to:
Develop and implement compliance and auditing programs; apply legal and administrative compliance policies to hospital or health systems; analyze data, draw logical conclusions, conduct independent audits, reviews, and make evaluations to ensure compliance issues and concerns are appropriately evaluated, investigated and resolved; recommend effective courses of action; communicate effectively in oral and written form; establish and maintain effective working relationships; conduct independent systems analyses of complex business processes.

Support Department of the Navy (DoN) and Department of Defense (DoD) Security Cooperation (SC), Security Assistance (SA) and Foreign Military Sales (FMS) assessments, staff organization, and administrative requirements.

Attend and actively participate in team meetings.

The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland’s mission is to foster the stability, integrity, and efficiency of the nation’s monetary, financial, and payment systems while representing the Fourth District perspectives.

As part of the nation’s central bank, we are a team of mission-driven professionals who are committed to serving with excellence. Our core values are: Build Trust Every Day, Own Our Actions, Collaborate with Intention, and Be Open to Change.

Conducts advanced analysis and policy directed research that contributes to internal publications, external publications, policy advising, and outreach. As part of a multidisciplinary and collaborative team of researchers and professionals, you will work in all areas of policy advising and support directly for the Bank President and senior Bank principles. We are part of the Executive function.

The Senior Policy analyst will analyze and research on issues that affect financial markets and monetary policy across a broad range of topic areas, expanding the bank’s capabilities to monitor and assess the impacts of market developments and functioning on policy. You will use database knowledge to compile statistical data, create data exploration tools, conduct initial data exploration on your own and work with senior staff members on their research. Strong ability to balance multiple projects and deadlines

new_jobs.title: Staff Technical Program Manager, IT Audit & Governance
new_jobs.description:
We're looking for a senior, hands-on leader to own IT audit and governance across all of our applications, infrastructure, and systems. You'll be accountable for keeping IT audit-ready every day: SOX ITGCs and ITACs, plus the broader audit and governance obligations that touch the technology stack (SOC reports, ISO, security and regulatory audits).

This role is about accountability and execution. You'll work with cross-functional IT leaders across Infrastructure, Engineering, Security, Cloud, Enterprise Applications, and Business Systems to make sure controls are owned, operated, evidenced, and remediated on time. You'll also be the primary IT liaison to Internal Audit, Finance/SOX PMO, and external auditors. You operate independently, influence without authority, and can speak credibly with an engineer about a CI/CD pipeline and with the CAO about a deficiency.

We're looking to speak with candidates based in Palo Alto or New York City for our hybrid working model.

What You'll Do

Own audit and governance across all IT

Own the audit and governance program across all IT applications, infrastructure, cloud platforms, and supporting systems
Maintain a complete inventory of systems, owners, and applicable audit and compliance obligations (SOX, SOC 1/SOC 2, ISO 27001, and other regulatory or customer requirements)
Build and run an IT audit calendar that coordinates SOX, internal audit, external audit, and compliance activities to reduce duplicate asks and audit fatigue
Establish governance standards, policies, and control frameworks that apply consistently across IT

Drive accountability and execution with IT leaders

Partner with cross-functional IT leaders to assign clear control and remediation ownership, with defined deadlines and escalation paths
Run regular governance forums and control health reviews with IT leadership, reporting status, risks, and overdue items
Hold teams accountable for timely control execution, evidence quality, and issue closure, escalating early when commitments slip
Translate audit and compliance requirements into practical work that engineering and infrastructure teams can adopt without slowing delivery

Own ITGC and ITAC compliance

Own the end-to-end SOX IT program: scoping inputs, control design, ownership, evidence, readiness testing, and issue management
Maintain the ITGC framework (access management, change management, IT operations, SDLC) across all in-scope applications, databases, operating systems, and cloud infrastructure
Own ITAC strategy and coverage with Finance and business-system owners: automated controls, configurations, interfaces, calculations, and approval workflows
Own IPE/report validation, ITAC baselines, and segregation of duties (SoD) across ERP and key financial applications

Design, operate, and strengthen controls

Design controls that are engineered into IT workflows (ticketing, CI/CD, IAM, CMDB) rather than layered on manually
Run readiness and self-assessment testing ahead of Internal Audit and external auditor testing
Rationalize overlapping controls across frameworks so one control and one piece of evidence can satisfy multiple requirements
Drive automation and continuous control monitoring to reduce manual effort and audit burden
Manage SOC 1/SOC 2 report reviews, CUECs, and third-party/vendor control dependencies

Drive remediation and issue management

Own the issue lifecycle across IT, from identification and root cause through remediation plan, validation, and closure
Prepare management's response to audit findings and provide the IT perspective on deficiency severity with Finance, Legal, and Internal Audit
Report control health and remediation status to IT leadership, the CAO, and the Audit Committee as needed

Be the IT face to auditors and the business

Serve as primary IT contact for Internal Audit and external auditors on scope, walkthroughs, evidence requests, and reliance strategy
Coordinate PBC requests, evidence standards, and timelines across IT teams
Train and enable control owners and IT leaders on audit requirements, evidence quality, and their responsibilities

Lead and elevate the program

Set standards for control documentation, evidence, and issue management across IT
Mentor analysts and guide co-source or outsourced resources
Contribute to emerging governance areas such as AI/emerging technology

What You'll Bring

Required

8-12+ years of experience in IT audit, SOX compliance, IT governance, or technology risk (Big 4, internal audit, or in-house IT GRC)
Deep, hands-on experience with SOX 404 ITGCs and ITACs in a public company
Working knowledge of COSO, COBIT, and PCAOB AS 2201, and how external auditors approach IT reliance and ITAC testing
Experience across modern technology environments: cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP), SaaS, ERP (e.g., Oracle, NetSuite, SAP), infrastructure, and identity/access platforms
Familiarity with other frameworks and audits (SOC 1/SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST) and how to harmonize them
Proven track record of owning programs end-to-end and driving accountability and execution across multiple teams and senior leaders without direct authority
Excellent communication and executive presence, including negotiating with auditors and briefing senior leadership
Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Accounting, Computer Science, or a related field

Preferred

CISA, CISSP, CIA, CPA, or equivalent certification
Experience with GRC and audit tools (e.g., AuditBoard, ServiceNow GRC, Workiva, Archer)
Data analytics skills (SQL, Python, Power BI/Tableau) for full-population testing and control monitoring
Experience in high-growth, SaaS, or technology company environments

new_jobs.title: Research Analyst I, Bioanalysis LBA
new_jobs.description:
For 75 years, Charles River employees have worked together to assist in the discovery, development and safe manufacture of new drug therapies. When you join our family, you will have a significant impact on the health and well-being of people across the globe. Whether your background is in life sciences, finance, IT, sales or another area, your skills will play an important role in the work we perform. In return, we’ll help you build a career that you can feel passionate about.

Job Overview

The Immunology and Immunochemistry disciplines support large molecule drug development using ligand binding assays (LBA), such as enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), to measure large molecules and their immune responses. The main types of assays include Pharmacokinetic (PK) assays to measure drug and Immunogenicity assay to measure anti-drug antibodies (ADA) and neutralizing antibodies (NAb). Other assay types also performed are branched DNA (bDNA) and cell-based assays. An array of platforms are used to support these assays that include spectrophotometer, Meso Scale Discovery (MSD), Luminex and Gyrolab. Utilizing these platforms/assays, the teams are responsible for the method development, validation and routine sample analysis in both the regulated and non-regulated space of non-clinical and clinical studies.

Responsibilities

Essential Functions (The fundamental Competencies/Skills & Responsibilities of the role (products and services provided/results accomplished) include, but are not limited to, those listed:

Efficiently perform and document all procedures, materials and results in compliance with applicable regulatory standards as applicable (protocols, methods, SOPs, etc.)
Demonstrate effective communication skills through informal discussions with peers, supervisor, and team
Assist with laboratory maintenance functions
Independently perform laboratory support functions such as labeling and solution preparationsAssist with maintaining study specific inventory of consumables with oversight
Write both study and non-study deviations with minimal oversight
Actively participate in process improvement initiatives with oversight
Develop critical thinking, troubleshooting and time management skills aligned with needs of the operational area
Assist in execution of routine sample analysis studies with oversight
Assist in execution of method validation projects with oversight as needed
Operate laboratory instruments with complete oversight
Assist with data analysis in appropriate software for at least one analytical platform
Performs all other related duties as assigned

Education

Job Requirements

Minimum of a Bachelor’s degree (BA/BS)

No Previous Experience Required

Ability to communicate verbally and in writing at all levels inside and outside the organization

Basic familiarity with Microsoft Office Suite

Computer skills, commensurate with Essential Functions, including the ability to learn a validated system

Ability to work extended hours beyond normal work schedule to include, but not limited to evenings, weekends, extended shifts, and/or extra shifts, sometimes on short notice

Ability to work under specific time constraints

Must be authorized to work in the United States without a sponsor visa, now or in the future.

Workplace Requirements

While performing the duties of this job, the employee must be able to perform general office and/or laboratory procedures, which require, talking, hearing, standing, or sitting for long periods of time, typing/entering data into a computer, using appropriate instruments, reaching with hands and arms, and wearing safety equipment (PPE) according to OSHA regulations and company standards.
Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.
General office working conditions, the noise level in the work environment is usually quiet.
While performing the duties of this job the employee may occasionally be required to wear protective clothing (goggles, face shield, surgical mask, cap, gloves, scrubs, boots), work near toxic or caustic chemicals, work with biohazards, and/or work with live animals with risk of exposure to allergens and/or zoonotic diseases.
The employee may occasionally be exposed to fumes or airborne particles, unpleasant odors, and/or wet, humid and/or extreme temperature conditions.

The pay rate for this role is $23.50/hour.

About Safety Assessment

Charles River is committed to helping our partners expedite their preclinical drug development with exceptional safety assessment services, state-of-the-art facilities and expert regulatory guidance. From individual specialty toxicology and IND enabling studies to tailored packages and total laboratory support, our deeply experienced team can design and execute programs that anticipate challenges and avoid roadblocks for a smooth, efficient journey to market. Each year approximately 300 investigational new drug (IND) programs are conducted in our Safety Assessment facilities.

About Charles River

Charles River is an early-stage contract research organization (CRO). We have built upon our foundation of laboratory animal medicine and science to develop a diverse portfolio of discovery and safety assessment services, both Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) and non-GLP, to support clients from target identification through preclinical development. Charles River also provides a suite of products and services to support our clients’ clinical laboratory testing needs and manufacturing activities. Utilizing this broad portfolio of products and services enables our clients to create a more flexible drug development model, which reduces their costs, enhances their productivity and effectiveness to increase speed to market.

With over 20,000 employees within 110 facilities in over 20 countries around the globe, we are strategically positioned to coordinate worldwide resources and apply multidisciplinary perspectives in resolving our client’s unique challenges. Our client base includes global pharmaceutical companies, biotechnology companies, government agencies and hospitals and academic institutions around the world.

At Charles River, we are passionate about our role in improving the quality of people’s lives. Our mission, our excellent science and our strong sense of purpose guide us in all that we do, and we approach each day with the knowledge that our work helps to improve the health and well-being of many across the globe. We have proudly worked on 80% of the drugs approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in the past five years.

We’re committed to providing benefits that elevate your quality of life. Based on your position these may include: bonus/incentives based on performance, 401K, paid time off, stock purchase program, Health and wellness coverage, employee and family wellbeing support programs, and work life balance flexibility.
